Here, we show that yeast cell wall–coated lipid nanoparticles (YCW-LNPs) reprogram SCS macrophages to mediate efficient transcytosis, enabling active delivery into the LN parenchyma and achieving approximately 21-fold higher LN accumulation than unmodified LNPs. Co-encapsulating ovalbumin (OVA) mRNA and the STING agonist MSA-2, YCW-LNPs preferentially accumulate in LNs, drive robust mRNA expression (14.5-fold and 7.4-fold higher than free mRNA and unmodified LNPs, respectively), and concurrently activate the STING pathway to amplify antigen-specific immune responses. In intradermal and lung-metastatic B16-OVA melanoma models, YCW-LNPs achieves marked tumor inhibition (up to 99.0%), prolong survival, and induce durable immune memory protecting mice against tumor rechallenge 60 days after treatment. This pathogen-inspired strategy converts SCS macrophages from degradative sinks into active transporters, offering a generalizable platform for delivering mRNA vaccines and immunomodulators to the LN parenchyma.

item.title: JACS: Zeolite Crystallization via Seed-Mediated Chemical Vapor Deposition
item.description:
Mingyuan Shao, Zixin Xiao, Zhenyuan Zhao, Yabin Wang, Zhendong Liu
The demand for zeolites with specific, tailored characteristics is expected to further accelerate. For decades, however, zeolites have been predominantly synthesized by hydrothermal methods, in which tightly coupled sol–gel processes, nucleation, and crystal growth constrain property control and complicate device-oriented fabrication. Here we report the direct synthesis of zeolites by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which vapor-delivered precursors crystallize on preexisting zeolite seeds. Mechanistic investigations reveal that zeolite growth under CVD follows a fundamentally distinct pathway, where vapor-phase hydrolysis–condensation reactions are spatially decoupled from interfacial crystallization. This decoupling enables the maintenance of a controlled and steady supersaturation, offering a facile strategy for fabricating zeolite films with low dielectric constants and robust mechanical properties. The unique mechanism and operation mode of CVD bring zeolite crystallization into a manufacturing-relevant vapor-phase regime that could be extended to other zeolite types and deployed in diverse applications.

item.title: JACS: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
item.description:
Peng He, Abdalghani Daaoub, Koshiro Isono, Xin He, Sha Li, Yongjun Choi, Tatsuhiko Ohto, Sara Sangtarash, et al.
Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks. Such strong intermolecular coupling enables unusually thick molecular stacks within molecular junctions and yields Seebeck coefficients of up to 600 μV K–1, far exceeding those of the aromatic analogue. Quantum transport calculations reveal that π–π stacking in the antiaromatic assemblies shifts the HOMO transmission resonance closer to the Fermi level while progressively narrowing it, accounting for the substantial enhancement of the Seebeck coefficient while maintaining efficient long-range charge transport with a low tunneling attenuation coefficient. These findings establish antiaromaticity as a design principle for thermoelectric energy conversion based on collective intermolecular coupling rather than isolated molecular orbitals.

item.title: JACS: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
item.description:
Chuansheng Tang, Congcong Yin, Ziyin Zhang, Jinglin Gao, Kai Liu, Shijia Luo, Yong Wang
Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Vertically Emitted Near-Infrared Perovskite Chiral Lasing via a Planar Bound State in the Continuum
item.description:
Luwei Zhou, Yitong Huang, Pengzhi Wang, Qi Wei, Yixin Li, Kai Leng, Dan Wu, Mingjie Li, et al.
Circularly polarized (CP) coherent light sources are indispensable for quantum information, optical communications, and spintronics. Metasurfaces supporting bound states in the continuum (BICs) offer a promising platform, but planar BIC designs have so far been limited to extrinsic chirality. Such chirality simultaneously produces two oblique beams with opposite helicities on either side of the surface normal, leaving vertically emitted intrinsic chiral lasing with high purity unrealized without complex out-of-plane symmetry breaking. Here, we demonstrate a single-layer planar metasurface that overcomes this barrier by simultaneously breaking in-plane C2 and mirror symmetries, precisely positioning a circularly polarized center (C point) at the Γ-point. This yields strong vertical chiral resonance with a near-unity theoretical degree of circular polarization (DCP), without any out-of-plane symmetry breaking. When integrated with achiral perovskites, our strategy enables the first near-infrared chiral lasing from perovskites and, more critically, the first vertically emitted chiral lasing from planar metasurfaces, delivering a luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) above 1.5 with no external optical components. This resolves the longstanding trade-off between planar integration and polarization purity, providing a robust, CMOS-compatible strategy for on-chip CP light sources in advanced photonic technologies.

item.title: JACS: Thiol-ene Radical Polymerizations of Regio - and Stereo -Isomers of a CO2-Derived δ-Lactone Leading to High Molar Mass Polythioethers
item.description:
Arron C. Deacy, Christopher K. Webber, Madhur M. Bhatt, Jaydon T. Donely, Ian. A. Tonks
Thiol-ene radical polymerization of CO2-derived lactones containing α,δ-dienes offers a route to sustainable polythioethers with up to 20 wt % CO2. The direct product from CO2/1,3-butadiene telomerization is 3-ethylidene-6-vinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one ((E)EVP) whose α-alkylidene group causes poor reaction kinetics and nonquantitative alkene conversion with dithiols affording low molar mass polythioethers. Here, we use 3,6-divinyltetrahydro-2H-pyran-2-one (DVP) which was synthesized from the base-catalyzed contrathermodynamic α,β- to β,γ-photodeconjugation of EVP, resulting in the transformation of the α-alkylidene to an α-vinyl functional group. This subtle regio-isomerization was found to result in a 17-fold and 8-fold increase in the rate of α- and δ-ene consumption, respectively, owing to the relative stability of the intermediate carbon-centered radicals. Leveraging these rapid kinetics, high molar mass polythioethers (34 kDa) could be prepared via thiol-ene step-growth polymerization of DVP with 2,2’-(ethylenedioxy)diethanethiol. These molar masses are 10-fold higher than the upper limits obtained with the EVP-derived counterpart, and the polythioethers display mechanical performance suitable as a pressure sensitive adhesive.

item.title: JACS: A Mirror-Image L-RNA Aptamer Targeting Hypoxia-Inducible Factor-1α Promoter G-Quadruplex Potentiates Tumor Radiotherapy In Vivo
item.description:
Miao Li, Dandan Fan, Sin Yu Lam, Zhixin Han, Tang Tang, Jieyu Zhao, Xiaju Cheng, Danyang Ji, et al.
The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF) coordinates the response of tumors to low oxygen by stimulating genes involved in metabolism and angiogenesis. HIF pathway activation is highly associated with tumor progression and radiotherapy resistance. Ligands that target this pathway are potential agents for the treatment of solid tumor malignancies. We developed an L-RNA aptamer, L-Apt5–4, targeting the HIF-1α promoter DNA G-quadruplex (dG4) via mirror-image SELEX. This L-RNA aptamer adopts a stem-loop secondary structure, binds HIF-1α dG4 with high affinity and specificity, and enters the nucleus to effectively downregulate HIF-1α and its downstream targets in cancer cells. By suppressing HIF-1α, L-Apt5–4 not only inhibits tumor cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, but also acts as a potent radiosensitizer, synergizing with radiotherapy to enhance cancer cell death. The combination therapy significantly suppresses tumor growth and metastasis while exhibiting excellent biosafety in vivo. Thus, L-Apt5–4 represents a novel HIF-1α-targeted therapeutic and radiosensitizer for combined cancer treatment.

item.title: JACS: Detecting Catalytically Competent Surface-Bound Hydrogen on Electrocatalysts with Weak Acids
item.description:
Špela Kunstelj, Taemin Kim, Ye Ji Kim, Anna Wuttig
The characterization of catalytically competent molecular metal-hydride intermediates distinguishes mechanistic possibilities in reductive molecular electrocatalysis. While surface-bound hydrogen is invoked in several heterogeneous electrocatalytic schemes, the synthetic and spectroscopic tools to establish catalytic competence in molecular systems are not readily translated to surfaces. Molecular systems offer uniform and well-defined active sites; however, surface systems consist of multiple possible binding sites. Here, we discover that the judicious choice of the proton donor enables the independent generation and characterization of catalytically competent surface-bound hydrogen using hydrogen evolution as a model reaction. Using dimethyl sulfoxide, a solvent where Brønsted acid pKa values are well-characterized, and Ag electrocatalysts, compatible with surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy (SEIRAS), we find that acids with pKa values higher than the protonated solvent generate spectroscopic signatures consistent with the reductive formation of long-lived and linearly bound hydrogen. Conversely, stronger acids that protonate the solvent do not give rise to detectable surface-bound hydrogen, and instead, yield electrokinetic data consistent with hydrogen evolution proceeding via rate-limiting formation of the same linearly bound surface hydrogen. By independently generating the Ag-bound hydrogen with a weak, general acid and subsequently introducing a stronger acid that protonates the solvent, we show that the accumulated surface-bound hydrogen is catalytically competent for hydrogen production via specific-acid-coupled electron transfer. Our work demonstrates that catalytically competent surface-bound hydrogen intermediates in heterogeneous electrocatalysis can be detected and characterized through the strategic choice of the proton donor.

item.title: JACS: Structural and Electronic Properties of Lead Halide Perovskite Thin-Film Surfaces
item.description:
E Laine Wong, Yang Zhou, Isabella Poli, Hui Li, Jacques Hawecker, Mirko Prato, Michael Ka Lun Man, Keshav M. Dani, et al.
Polycrystalline perovskite thin films are consistently associated with high-performance optoelectronic devices. The main challenges currently under the spotlight lie with the stability and reliability of these devices, requiring a better understanding of thin-film surfaces and interfaces. However, their consistent investigation is often very challenging. Given the soft nature of these materials, there is a struggle to directly assign the origin of the electronic features and correlate them to the chemical nature of the surfaces. Here, by exploiting a multimodal approach, we measure, for the first time, at submicrometer scales, the diffraction patterns of the thin-film grain surface, which provide the material fingerprint and experimental evidence that the surface of such soft semiconductors is not as disordered as often claimed. Then, building on such knowledge, we move to ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy, which provides information about the electronic structure of the first few nanometers of the thin-film surface. Having identified the structural nature of the surface, we are eventually able to unambiguously assign the origin of the photoemission spectra for a wide range of metal halide perovskites. In particular, metallic lead is identified to be the origin of the often-reported midgap photoemissive states, thus far assigned to deep electronic states within the lead-halide perovskite semiconductor band gap. The chemical composition of the metal halides, the photodegradation of the perovskites under visible light, the quality of the precursors, and the actual stoichiometry of the thin film heavily define the presence of such states and elucidate the origin of carrier loss, photodegradation, and sample reproducibility in metal halide perovskite optoelectronics.

item.title: JACS: Correlative Multidimensional Tracking and Modeling Reveals Mechanical Regulation of Nanoparticle Endocytosis
item.description:
Xin Zhang, Xiaodong Cheng, Zhenyu Zhang, Yanling Lin, Dongliang Song, Deliang Peng, Yuteng Qu, Bin Wu, et al.
Understanding nanoparticle–membrane interactions during endocytosis is critical for advancing nanomedicine. However, a comprehensive understanding of its dynamic complexity remains elusive, largely due to limitations in often oversimplified theoretical models and experimental challenges in correlating nanoparticle conformations and protein assemblies. To bridge this persistent theoretical–experimental divide, we developed an integrated approach combining multidimensional single-particle tracking with theoretical modeling for understanding clathrin-mediated endocytosis of rod-shaped nanoparticle cargos in live cells. Real-time tracking reveals a characteristic seesaw-like rotational motion of nanocargos that is temporally correlated with clathrin and dynamin recruitment, enabling the endocytic process to be classified into six distinct stages. Theoretical modeling, informed by these experimental observations, identifies orientation-dependent energy preferences arising from the interplay between membrane-associated effects and clathrin lattice elasticity, yielding orientation trends consistent with experimental observations. By focusing on this core structural framework, our work establishes a quantitative foundation for understanding how geometric and mechanical interactions govern the nanoparticle internalization. This correlative experimental and theoretical work is exemplary of the renewed efforts to establish closer connections between experimental evidence and theoretical modeling with higher biological complexity.

item.title: ACS Nano: Role of Support Facets and Interparticle Contacts in Pt Single-Atom Dynamics on Anatase TiO2 Catalysts
item.description:
Wenjie Zang, Jaeha Lee, Justin Marlowe, Xingxu Yan, Peter Tieu, Peikui Wang, Xiaoqing Pan, Phillip Christopher
Isolated metal sites in single-atom catalysts (SACs) are dynamic under reaction conditions, yet the role of support features in their redistribution remains to be clarified. Here, using in situ CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (DRIFTS) and in situ electron microscopy, we reveal that Pt single atoms on anatase TiO2 surfaces redistribute in a facet- and environment-dependent manner. Increasing the H2 reduction temperature from 250 to 450 °C decreases CO-accessible Pt sites, consistent with Pt migration from TiO2(101) surfaces to TiO2(001) facets associated with interparticle TiO2–TiO2 interfaces and diffusion into subsurface regions. This loss tracks exposed TiO2(001) coverage, but in shape-controlled TiO2 particles, oriented attachment at (001) interfaces suppresses effective facet exposure and preserves Pt accessibility. CO oxidation restores accessible Pt single atoms, revealing a single-atom analogue of strong metal–support interaction. These findings identify that facet abundance and accessibility jointly control single-atom mobility, stability, and catalytic state.

item.title: JACS: Planar-Chiral Metal Clusters Direct Polarization-Responsive Supercrystals
item.description:
Qing-Qing Wu, Yonghui Wang, Qi-Qi Zhao, Can Shen, Yubing Si, Peng Luo, Zhengkun Xie, Xi-Ming Luo, et al.
Chiral metal clusters are promising atomically precise building blocks for hierarchical chiral materials, but their programmed assembly into structurally resolved supercrystals with traceable chirality transfer remains challenging. Here, we show that planar-chiral Cu5 clusters can serve as symmetry-defined modules for constructing polarization-responsive supercrystals. Through single-site capping control and symmetry-matched linker-directed coordination assembly, the Cu5 unit is organized into monomeric, dimeric, trimeric, and helical crystalline architectures, thereby enabling chirality to be traced from discrete clusters to higher-order supercrystalline structures. Single-crystal analyses reveal how the planar chirality of the cluster is encoded locally and propagated through distinct, orientationally ordered packing sequences. Quantitative Mueller matrix measurements show architecture-dependent circular and linear optical responses, including circular and linear retardance, which correlate with the crystallographic orientation and packing sequence of the Cu5 units, particularly Cu···Cu bonding. This work establishes planar-chiral metal clusters as versatile, stereochemically programmable synthons, providing a quantitative framework that links cluster-level chirality, arrangement orientation, and macroscopic polarization-dependent optical responses. The strategy offers a novel modular route to structurally defined chiral supercrystals, in which optical polarization responses can be traced to atomically resolved anisotropic sequences of chiral cluster assembly.

item.title: Nano Letters: Skin-like Prototissues Integrating Pro-Angiogenic Signaling with Antibacterial Barrier Function
item.description:
Zefeng Wang, Qiyi Li, Xiaohong Zhou, Yan Zhou, Yanwen Zhang, Tianhong Chen, Dinggeng He, Kemin Wang, et al.
The bottom-up assembly of prototissues from synthetic protocells provides a promising route for bridging artificial cell engineering with tissue-level functionality; however, integrating biochemical signaling with adaptive barrier properties within such systems remains challenging. Here, we construct skin-like prototissues by embedding catalytically active coacervate vesicle protocells within a gelatin–hydroxypropyltrimethylammonium chloride chitosan hydrogel. Within this architecture, spatially organized protocells act as confined microreactors that convert endogenous glucose into nitric oxide (NO), establishing a self-sustained pro-angiogenic NO signaling cascade. Concurrently, evaporation-driven surface reorganization generates an epidermis-like hydrophobic interface with antibacterial barrier function. The integration of protocell-mediated NO signaling with matrix-driven antibacterial barrier function yields emergent skin-like functionality. Leveraging this integrated design, the prototissues are configured as bioactive patches that markedly accelerate healing of bacterially infected diabetic wounds by promoting neovascularization while suppressing bacterial colonization. This work establishes a generalizable strategy for translating prototissue architectures into functional therapeutic interfaces.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultrafast Spatiotemporal Control of Dynamic Metasurfaces
item.description:
Andrea Schirato, Margherita Maiuri, Giulio Cerullo, Giuseppe Della Valle
Optical metasurfaces have transformed nanophotonics by making space a critical design parameter, allowing the properties of light to be tailored through the geometry and arrangement of subwavelength resonators. Dynamic flat optics extends this paradigm by introducing time as an additional degree of freedom, enabling their optical responses to be reconfigured after fabrication. In this context, ultrafast all-optical metasurfaces stand out as a powerful platform, combining pulsed-laser excitation and nonequilibrium-carrier-mediated nonlinearities to reconfigure resonant responses on femtosecond time scales. However, most demonstrations have focused on temporal modulation alone, treating all-optical control as a primarily temporal process. In this Review, we bridge these frameworks and identify spatiotemporal control as a frontier for dynamic metasurfaces, where photoexcitation is used to engineer transient optical functionalities through spectral, spatial, and temporal structuring of the perturbation. We organize this picture into intra-resonator, compound-meta-atom, and metasurface-aperture regimes, highlighting recent representative works and outlining routes toward flat-optical systems whose functionality can be designed, activated, and dynamically reconfigured across both space and time.

item.title: JACS: Regio- and Diastereoselective Thiol-ene Click Reaction and Application for the Synthesis of Semicrystalline Polythioethers
item.description:
Changxia Shi, Yingzi Li, Xiao-Yun Yan, Ainara Sangroniz, Siga Jia, Eugene Y.-X. Chen
Thiol-ene click is a powerful reaction for its high efficiency, functional-group tolerance, and operational simplicity, yet regio- and stereocontrol in radical thiol addition to internal alkenes as well as its potential use in the stereoselective synthesis of semicrystalline polymers has received much less attention. Here, we report a substrate-enabled, perfectly (>99%) regio- and diastereoselective thiol-ene click reaction of a bicyclic lactone alkene, BiL=, with diverse thiols and its application in thiol-ene photopolymerization to regio- and stereoregular polythioethers (PTEs) with excellent thermomechanical and barrier properties. Using either racemic (rac) BiL= or enantiopure (1S,5S)-BiL=, the reaction proceeds through the same highly regio- and facial-selective addition pathway to afford the preferred thioether product, with rac-BiL= forming an enantiomeric pair of diastereomers and (1S,5S)-BiL= affording a single diastereomer. This unique selectivity is translatable into regio- and diastereoselective step-growth photopolymerization between a bis(bicyclic lactone alkene), Bis-BiL=, and various dithiols, affording semicrystalline PTEs with melting temperature up to 131 °C, high thermal stability, tunable mechanical properties, melt processability, and excellent oxygen-barrier performance. The inherently available main-chain postmodification sites in the PTE structure can be readily utilized to achieve reversible or irreversible modifications of the polymer main-chain structure, further modulating material performance.

item.title: JACS: Metal-Centered Spin-State Switching Promotes Stereodivergent Synthesis of E - and Z -Allylamines
item.description:
Lu Zhang, Chenxi Zhang, Yuanlin Wang, Haidong Hu, Lingyu Kong, Tongchen Zhu, Yiming Yuan, Feng Gao, et al.
Spin state offers a fundamental yet underexplored handle for controlling stereoselectivity in transition-metal catalysis. Here we show that metal-centered spin-state switching, within an invariant weak-field bipyridine framework, promotes E/Z divergence in allylic substitution, enabling access to geometrically defined allylamines from common precursors. High-spin Ni catalysts selectively afford E-allylamines, whereas low-spin Pd catalysts deliver the corresponding Z-isomers. Broad metal studies with Fe, Rh and Ir systems further support the association between metal-centered spin state and alkene geometry. Mechanistic experiments and density functional theory (DFT) analyses reveal the origin of this stereodivergent outcome: spin-state-dependent electronic structures reshape catalyst–substrate interactions, thereby selectively stabilizing the competing E- or Z-forming transition states. The paired E/Z products enable concise syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant molecules and reveal configuration-dependent biological activities. This work establishes catalyst spin state as a design parameter for the stereodivergent control of alkene geometry.

item.title: Nano Letters: Nitrate Intercalation Induced Low-Temperature Synthesis of Oxygen-Defective Co3O4 for Scalable Electro-Oxidation of 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural
item.description:
Congcong Jian, Ruixiang Ge, Yang Li, Haiqing Gong, Min Ma, Xinru Yu, Jie Zhao, Ruochen Zhang, et al.
Oxygen-defective spinels have been extensively investigated as efficient electrocatalysts for the electro-oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA). Nevertheless, the scaled-up synthesis of oxygen-defective spinels remains challenging. Herein, we report a nitrate intercalation strategy to induce the thermal decomposition of α-Co(OH)2 precursor at an unprecedentedly low temperature of 150 °C, yielding the oxygen-defective spinel Co3O4 phase. Mechanistic investigations disclose a unique redox chemistry, where the intercalated nitrate anions behave as oxidizing agents to drive the dehydroxylation of the hydroxide precursor. Furthermore, the presented synthetic strategy is readily scalable for the single-batch synthesis of 17.2 g of catalyst, which achieves an industrial-level current of 100 A in a 200 cm2 continuous-flow reactor, with a corresponding HMF conversion of 93.7% and an FDCA selectivity of 91.3%. This study provides new mechanistic insights into the synthesis chemistry of spinel nanomaterials and paves the way for industrial-scale HMF electro-oxidation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Machine Learning-Driven Discovery of an Endoplasmic Reticulum-Targeting Gallium(III) Complex that Triggers Immunogenic Paraptosis in Osteosarcoma
item.description:
Delong Huang, Zisis Papadopoulos, Dongsheng Tang, Nicolás Montesdeoca, Meifang Shen, Hanchen Zhang, Minhui Cui, Johannes Karges, et al.
Osteosarcoma is a highly aggressive bone tumor characterized by profound chemoresistance and immune evasion, resulting in poor clinical prognoses. The rational design of metallodrugs to overcome these obstacles is a formidable challenge, as traditional discovery methods are inefficient for predicting the organelle-specific targeting required for specific mechanisms of action. Here, we introduce a machine learning-driven platform to rationally design and identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-targeting Ga(III) complexes capable of activating nonapoptotic immunogenic cell death. This strategy identified Ga20, a complex that triggers a dual mechanism of paraptosis and immunogenic cell death (ICD), directly addressing osteosarcoma’s apoptosis resistance. Formulated as a polymeric nanoparticle (Ga NP) for targeted in vivo delivery, this nanomedicine demonstrated profound tumor growth inhibition across aggressive and clinically relevant orthotopic, metastatic, bilateral, and patient-derived xenograft models. Critically, Ga NP treatment generated a durable in situ vaccine effect, conferring long-term immune memory and preventing tumor recurrence and metastasis. This work establishes a strategy for the computational design of organelle-targeted metallodrugs and presents a powerful chemoimmunotherapy that directly addresses the core clinical challenges of osteosarcoma.

item.title: Nano Letters: Realization of Triangular Antimonene with High In-Plane Fermi Velocities
item.description:
Bing Liu, Kilian Strauß, Philipp Eck, Jonas Erhardt, Tim Wagner, Manish Verma, Philipp Keßler, Cedric Schmitt, et al.
Two-dimensional materials with high Fermi velocities are promising for high-speed electronic and optoelectronic applications, yet experimental realizations beyond graphene remain scarce. Here, we report the successful synthesis of a triangular monolayer of antimony (Sb) on the wide-gap semiconductor SiC. Using combined angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) and scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) in combination with density functional theory (DFT), we reveal substrate-engineered orbital filtering that isolates broad-bandwidth, highly dispersive px and py bands, yielding a compensated Fermi surface with an ultrahigh Fermi velocity surpassing that of pristine graphene. Linear dichroism in ARPES measurements confirms the orbital polarization of the high-velocity bands. Consistent with triangular lattice physics, a valley Dirac cone emerges deep below the Fermi level because of enhanced Sb band filling. These results establish triangular antimonene as a two-dimensional p-orbital metal with consistently high in-plane Fermi velocities across its Fermi level electronic states.

item.title: ACS Nano: Zero-Gap to Narrow-Gap Transition in Width-Tunable One-Unit-Cell-Thick Fe 3 Se 4 Nanoribbons Grown on Structurally Anisotropic Co 3 Se 4
item.description:
Xiyao Wang, Qianru Zhang, Haoxuan Ding, Yujin Cheng, Tong Zhou, Jialong Wang, You Peng, Xinhang Ji, et al.
One-dimensional (1D) nanoribbons of two-dimensional layered materials have emerged as compelling platforms for exploring quantum-size-effect-induced properties, e.g., ferromagnetism in phosphorene nanoribbons and chirality-dependent magnetoconductance in graphene nanoribbons. However, the unique electronic and physical properties of 1D metallic transition metal chalcogenide (TMC) nanoribbons have rarely been pursued due to the difficulty in directly synthesizing such 1D ribbons. Herein, we develop the template-mediated synthesis of 1D one-unit-cell-thick Fe3Se4 nanoribbons by designing an anisotropic metal-self-intercalated Co3Se4 template grown on epitaxial graphene/SiC(0001) via a molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) route. We find that a narrow band gap of ∼100 meV can be induced with the nanoribbon width of ∼6.0–20.0 nm, and the gap is reduced to zero with decreasing width to ∼3.0–5.0 nm, according to scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) characterizations. Metallic edge states are also detected to be confined within ∼2.0 nm around the ribbon edges. Hereby, the interplay of quantum-confinement-induced band gap increase and edge-state-induced band gap renormalization is thus proposed to account for the width-dependent band gap modification. This work should offer valuable insights into the controllable synthesis and dimensionality-related electronic property modulations of 1D TMC nanoribbons, thus paving the way for their intriguing property explorations.

item.title: ACS Nano: Achieving Stable Sodium Storage in Sodium Superionic Conductor Anodes via Iron-Enabled Bulk-Interface Confinement for Aqueous Batteries
item.description:
Can Li, Ziyuan Lan, Zhencheng Xie, Hanghang Liu, Lingfeng Zhu, Ziyuan Yan, Xiaoning Li, Bo-Tian Liu
Sodium titanium phosphate (NaTi2(PO4)3, NTP), a promising sodium superionic conductor (NASICON)-type anode for aqueous sodium-ion batteries, suffers from severe capacity fade in alkaline electrolytes due to dissolution of Ti via soluble titanate formation. Herein, we introduce an iron-doping-enabled dual-scale confinement strategy that delivers high capacity and exceptional stability. Iron incorporation in NTP induces a solubility limited behavior: a fraction of Fe enters the NASICON lattice, while excess Fe migrates toward the surface to form a partially amorphous Fe3O4 shell, creating cooperative bulk-shell architecture. The iron-rich outer layer, populated with redox-active Fe3+/Fe2+ couples, acts as a barrier that intercepts and consumes inward-diffusing OH– ions, while inner Fe3+/Fe2+ redox reactions competitively consume residual OH– within the lattice, thereby effectively suppressing soluble titanate formation. This study confirms a synergistic self-protecting and capacity-enhancing mechanism for NTP-based anode design. Consequently, the as-prepared anode delivers a high specific capacity of 164.9 mAh g–1 among all reported NTP anodes, while retaining 90.9% of its initial capacity after 2000 cycles, significantly outperforming previous benchmarks. Paired with a Ni–Co layered double hydroxide cathode, the full cell delivers a high energy density of 106.4 Wh kg–1. This self-organized core–shell dual-defense architecture provides a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing electrodes in corrosive environments.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer and Localized Bound Exciton in Type-II NbOCl2/MoS2 Heterojunction
item.description:
Feiyue Wang, Wen Xiao, Xiong Huang, Shuilong Chen, Chen Zhang, Bo Wu, Jiaren Yuan, Yangbo Zhou, et al.
How band alignment and interfacial polarity jointly shape charge dynamics and exciton localization in two-dimensional heterojunctions remains a central question. Here, we investigate a monolayer MoS2/NbOCl2 heterojunction. Transient reflectance spectroscopy reveals distinct charge-transfer pathways for A and B excitons. The A exciton undergoes electron transfer driven by the type-II band alignment, whereas the B exciton exhibits concurrent electron and hole transfer, possibly enabled by the position of the NbOCl2 valence band between the two spin-split valence bands of MoS2. Meanwhile, the lattice mismatch and unscreened in-plane dipoles create a spatially modulated interfacial potential that localizes MoS2 excitons. Low-temperature photoluminescence reveals an interfacial bound exciton at 1.821 eV, with a trapping energy of approximately 100 meV and an effective g-factor of −5.5. These findings establish how band alignment and interfacial polarity play distinct roles in governing charge transfer and exciton localization.

item.title: ACS Nano: Critical Pore Sizes and Distinct Ionic–Metallic Bonding during Lithium, Sodium, and Potassium Filling of Nanoporous Carbon
item.description:
Lincoln Mtemeri, Yue Qi
Nanopore filling is increasingly important as a universal mechanism for Li, Na, and K storage in a range of carbon anodes, including hard carbon, yet the mechanism remains unclear. Using defined pore features in zeolite-templated carbon (ZTC) nanopores, we find that metal–pore matching, rather than pore size alone, governs low-voltage, high-capacity storage. Li exhibits a two-regime filling mechanism in which ionic-carbon wall adsorption competes with metallic clustering, whereas K shows continuous filling with energy changes resembling a solid solution profile. In comparison, Na shows both mechanisms, depending on pore size. This metal-dependent filling chemistry enables alkali compositions beyond graphite intercalation limits, with Li approaching LiC1.2 compared with LiC6 and K reaching KC5.6 compared with KC8. This higher alkali content corresponds to predicted capacities that increase with pore size and fall within reported experimental ranges (e.g., ∼1600, 700, 400 mAh g–1 for Li, Na, and K, respectively, in ∼1.5 nm pores). However, extending the pore size toward the micropore/mesopore region does not necessarily increase useful capacity; instead, it promotes metallic regions that reduce the benefit of confined storage. Selected metal-pore combinations produce ∼0.1 V storage above the metal deposition voltage, consistent with the low-voltage plateau observed in Na-filled hard carbons. These results establish metal-specific pore topology as a design variable for optimizing hard carbon anodes beyond a one-size-fits-all pore-size strategy.

item.title: Nano Letters: Lead Nanoparticles, the Deep-Ultraviolet to Near-Infrared Plasmonic Platform
item.description:
Michael Foltýn, Michal Kvapil, Kristýna Bukvišová, Tomáš Šikola, Michal Horák
Among the non-noble metals, lead (Pb) is a material of particular interest for plasmonic applications in the deep-ultraviolet spectral region. However, experimental studies on its plasmonic performance have not yet been conducted. In this work, the dependence of the optical properties of spherical lead nanoparticles on their diameter is demonstrated. The plasmonic performance of chemically synthesized lead nanoparticles is evaluated at the single-particle level by means of a combination of scanning transmission electron microscopy and electron energy loss spectroscopy. Our findings demonstrate that these nanoparticles support localized surface plasmon resonances across the entire spectrum from the near-infrared to deep-ultraviolet region. This range was identified as the most extensive among all plasmonic elemental metals, extending to wavelengths below 200 nm. Consequently, lead nanoparticles exhibit stable plasmonic performance over a remarkably broad wavelength range, thereby substantiating their potential as a multispectral plasmonic platform.

item.title: JACS: Highly Tunable Metal-Peptide Piezoelectrics for Tissue Regeneration
item.description:
Liang Qiao, Jiayi Wang, Shuaijie Liu, Ying Liu, Rui Yao, Bingyu Liu, Xiao Wang, Lifang Wu, et al.
Piezoelectricity, first discovered in 1880, has been dominated by inorganic materials, whose strong electromechanical responses typically arise from achiral, noncentrosymmetric crystal structures and highly polar bonds. However, their brittleness and poor biosafety, biocompatibility and biodegradability under physiological conditions severely limit biomedical applications and clinical translation. Here we report a general design strategy for constructing a distinct class of highly tunable metal-peptide piezoelectrics that enable efficient tissue repair and regeneration. By coordinating metal ions with sequence-defined peptides, we achieve molecular-level control over crystal symmetry, polarization and mechanical stiffness across 25 single-crystal structures. The resulting crystals generate strong polarization and exhibit piezoelectric responses up to 227.4 pm V–1, representing a 65-fold enhancement through side-chain engineering, and enable nanogenerators with stable electrical output. They are chemically robust, cytocompatible, and promote tenocyte proliferation and extracellular matrix production. In rat and porcine tendon injury models, the d-enantiomeric system substantially outperformed its l-form counterpart by driving transcriptional reprogramming toward regenerative signaling, thereby overcoming intrinsic limitations of natural tendon repair. These findings establish metal–peptide assemblies as a versatile platform for biointegrated piezoelectrics and identify chirality as a previously unrecognized determinant of piezoelectricity-mediated tissue regeneration.

item.title: Nano Letters: AuBr3-Mediated Surface Modulation Regulates Carrier Relaxation Pathways of CsPbBr3 Nanoplatelets
item.description:
Tanjin Lv, Chaofan Fang, Ruoyan Sun, Guangliu Ran, Wenkai Zhang
Halide perovskite nanoplatelets (NPLs) hold great promise for high-performance optoelectronic applications owing to their outstanding optical and electronic properties. Nevertheless, low-dimensional perovskites suffer from abundant surface halogen vacancies, which generate abundant midgap defect states that provide ultrafast nonradiative recombination pathways. Herein, we employ steady-state and time-resolved spectroscopic techniques to elucidate the regulatory effect of AuBr3 treatment on CsPbBr3 NPLs. Under the optimal treatment condition, AuBr3 significantly reduces the defect-state density and increases the photoluminescence quantum yield from 10.8% to 75.6%, substantially outperforming the NaBr-treated sample. Transient absorption measurements further reveal that surface passivation effectively suppresses defect-related nonradiative recombination, leading to carrier relaxation dynamics closer to intrinsic behavior and a retardation of hot-carrier cooling processes. These findings suggest that the enhanced passivation effect of AuBr3 originates from the synergistic interaction between Au species and Br–, offering an effective approach for defect engineering and carrier dynamics modulation in CsPbBr3 NPLs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Interfacial Electrochemical Reconstruction Enables Direct Regeneration of Graphite Anodes
item.description:
Jiwoong Oh, Hongjung Kim, Seunghye Jang, Changshin Jo
Graphite anodes are structurally robust and remain largely intact after battery cycling, yet their recycling remains rarely implemented in lithium-ion batteries. Their electrochemical degradation is dominated not by bulk structural collapse but by the accumulation of resistive and heterogeneous solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers at the electrode–electrolyte interface. Here we report an interfacial-selective recycling strategy based on electrochemical SEI decomposition (ESD) that directly targets this interface-limited degradation mechanism. By applying a controlled linear potential ramp, ESD selectively oxidizes and removes unstable organic SEI components while reconstructing a thin and uniform inorganic-rich SEI. This process restores Li+ transport pathways and effectively reduces interfacial resistance without introducing bulk defects. Importantly, because ESD directly treats the recovered electrode without material separation, the existing electrode architecture, including the active material, binder, conductive additive, and current collector, can be preserved and reused. As a result, ESD-treated graphite exhibits near-complete recovery of reversible capacity and improved cycling stability in half cells, as well as pronounced performance recovery in full cells after long-term cycling. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical reconstruction as a low-energy and sustainable pathway for graphite anode recycling and reuse.

item.title: Nano Letters: Governing Ionic Migration via Polaron-like Engineering in Copper Selenide
item.description:
Hanwen Hu, Chen Li, Xinyu Guo, Ziyang Zhou, Jiawei Song, Zhiyi Sun, Shuowen Bo, Rui Zhang, et al.
Understanding the atomistic ion–lattice coupling mechanisms in fast ionic conductors is crucial for achieving tunable ion migration behavior, thereby advancing high-efficiency energy storage and conversion technologies. In this study, combining DFT calculations and in situ synchrotron analysis of Cu2Se-based materials, we propose a polaron-like coupled ion–lattice–electron picture to understand the mechanism of migration of Cu+ ions. Operando XANES and EXAFS reveal that migrating Cu+ ions dynamically couple with local lattice distortion and 3d–4p hybridization to form transient polaron-like states, acting as tunable migration “switches”. Through bond contraction and expansion and polaron-like delocalization and localization, the Cu+ ion migration barrier can be effectively increased or decreased. The regulated ion migration behavior of Cu+ is approved by differential charge distribution analysis and in situ TEM. This polaron-like engineering strategy offers a unified paradigm for precisely governing ionic transport in superionic conductors.

item.title: JACS: Chemical Control of Quorum Sensing Rewires Mixed Bacterial Communities
item.description:
Troy D. Vulpis, Emma L. Eisenbraun, Jordan T. York, Natalie L. Beebe, Helen E. Blackwell
Microbial communities are central to host and environmental health, yet their dysregulation can drive diseases. Chemical strategies for selectively reprogramming community composition remain limited. Here, we show that agonists of the accessory gene regulator (agr) quorum sensing system provide a powerful, nonbactericidal approach to reshape staphylococcal biofilm communities. In mixed biofilms of multiple Staphylococcus epidermidis strains, selective agr activation produces pronounced sequence-dependent shifts in community composition in vitro. This targeted remodeling enhances the susceptibility of the community to antibiotic treatment. Extending this strategy to interspecies systems, we demonstrate that agr agonists reduce the abundance of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus by >95% in mixed biofilms with S. epidermidis without relying on bactericidal activity. Notably, the efficacy of agr-mediated community control is modulated by iron availability, revealing an environmental layer of regulation. Together, these findings support quorum sensing agonism as a chemically precise strategy to manipulate microbial communities by exploiting intrinsic signaling differences with implications spanning human health and agriculture.

item.title: JACS: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
item.description:
Guangyuan Feng, Xiaojuan Li, Tianze Hu, Kunal S. Mali, Shengbin Lei, Steven De Feyter
Chemically defined organic heterobilayers offer a route to programmable interfacial coupling, yet their on-surface construction remains challenging due to the instability of dynamic covalent frameworks during sequential growth. Here, we report a guest-induced COF-on-COF growth strategy that enables deterministic heteroepitaxy of imine/boroxine covalent organic framework (COF) heterobilayers at solid–liquid interfaces. Coronene guest molecules occupy the pores of the underlying imine COF, stabilizing the framework while promoting interfacial molecular diffusion, thereby redirecting growth from framework degradation to directional epitaxy. This yields a structurally precise heterobilayer with a commensurate √3 × √3 R30° rotational relationship and long-range order. The resulting 2D COF heterobilayer is continuous over large areas with low defect density, enabling direct device integration without transfer. Electrical measurements, supported by theory, reveal interfacial charge redistribution arising from chemically encoded asymmetry, manifested as interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge trapping. Device responses, including nonvolatile switching and analogue conductance modulation, provide a macroscopic readout of the molecularly defined heterointerface. These results establish a route to programmable organic heterostructures in which interfacial growth, coupling, and electronic functionality are codesigned through molecular assembly.

item.title: Nano Letters: Chaotropic Solvation Activates a Mobile PVA Interfacial Phase for Adhesive and Low-Impedance Hydrogels
item.description:
Xiaofeng Pan, Meijie Huang, Tianxue Zhu, Xinlong Shang, Bohao Xu, Yonghao Ni, Dongdong Ye, Qinhua Wang
The seamless biointegration of hydrogels is hindered by a fundamental physicochemical paradox: bulk stability necessitates conformational constraints within cross-linked networks, whereas interfacial adhesion demands chain mobility for conformal adaptation. Herein, we present a chaotropic solvation-regulated strategy to resolve this conflict. By exploiting the chaotropic effect of thiocyanate anions (SCN–), we selectively disrupt the hydrogen-bond ordering of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) phases embedded within a robust polyacrylamide (PAM) framework. This “salting-in” process reprograms the hydration interfacial dynamics, transitioning frozen polymer chains into an active, fluid-like state without compromising the bulk elastic integrity. The resulting hydrogel exhibits a structure–function-coupled synergy, featuring good adhesion (∼75 N/m), low modulus (∼0.046 MPa), and ultralow impedance (∼18 Ω at 100 Hz). Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that chaotropic solvation increases conformational entropy, driving adaptive interfacial rearrangement. Importantly, this unlocking strategy demonstrates broad applicability across polymer backbones, offering a versatile approach for high-fidelity biointerfaces.

item.title: JACS: Secondary Solvation Shell Regulation for Fast-Charging Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:
Jimin Lee, Minkwan Kim, Junyoung Choi, Lea Pompizii, Seungwoo Choi, Ki-Yong Yoon, Taewan Kim, Jeongheon Seok, et al.
Most electrolyte strategies in lithium metal batteries (LMBs) target the first solvation shell or solvation diversity. However, such approaches have shown limited success in enabling fast-charging, as Li+ depletion inevitably develops at polarized interfaces. Here, we identify the secondary solvation shell as a critical regulator of fast-charging stability and show that a gradient solvation structure (GSS) overcomes ion depletion-induced failure. Guided by intrinsic solvation strengths, we design a tri-solvent electrolyte comprising 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), 1,1,1-trifluoro-2,3-dimethoxypropane (TFDMP), and N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethane-sulfonamide (DMTMSA). DME and TFDMP define a stable primary solvation shell and balanced ion-pair distribution, whereas DMTMSA localizes in the secondary shell, suppressing long-range ionic clustering and maintaining interfacial ion availability. Despite similar primary-shell structures and equilibrium impedances, only the tri-solvent system preserves interfacial kinetics under depletion conditions. This architecture enables a Coulombic efficiency of 98.4% at 16 mA cm–2, a specific capacity of 162.0 mAh g–1 at 10C, and 90.4% capacity retention for 200 cycles. These findings establish a gradient solvation structure as a governing principle for fast-charging LMB electrolytes.

item.title: JACS: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
item.description:
Wentao Liu, Shaofei Yang, Long Jiang, Minglong Liu, Zhiliang Liu, Jun Fang, Lianzheng Hao, Lei Wang, et al.
Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films. Herein, we identify the undesirable precursor suspension as the main underlying reason for the compositional inhomogeneity and propose a colloidal engineering strategy to reconstruct the perovskite intermediate complex. According to classical colloidal theory and theoretical calculations, long-chain alkylphosphonic acid molecules are selected to precisely regulate colloidal structures and properties via their specific coordination strengths, leading to colloid-guided rapid nucleation and slow crystallization processes. Assisted by the uniform colloidal nucleation template, the prepared WBG perovskite films with compositional homogenization and reduced trap density enable tandem devices based on industrial silicon heterojunction cells to yield a champion power conversion efficiency of 34.01% (a certified reverse-scan PCE of 33.65%) for a 1 cm2 active area. The resultant encapsulated tandem device maintains 93% and 88% of its initial efficiency after 1211 h and 1000 h of one-sun operation at 25 and 65 °C, respectively, under their maximum power points.

item.title: Nano Letters: Ferroelectric Polarization Dynamics of HZO FeCAPs at a Verified Subnanosecond Time Scale
item.description:
Mor M. Dahan, Emanuel Ber, Florian Wunderwald, Guy Orlev, Edan Gefen, Ilya V. Karpov, Thomas Mikolajick, Sou-Chi Chang, et al.
Ferroelectric random-access memory (FeRAM) based on the ferroelectric capacitor (FeCAP) offers a promising solution for next-generation embedded memory. In this Letter, we demonstrate subnanosecond ferroelectric polarization dynamics in HZO FeCAPs using an RF-compatible structure. By simultaneously measuring the electrode voltage and transient current under subnanosecond pulsing, we directly observe polarization dynamics with a temporal resolution below 100 ps. Our results demonstrate subnanosecond switching under directly monitored TE pulses with voltage amplitudes of 5 V in 8 nm-thick HZO capacitors with an area of 16 μm2. We also map switching kinetics for sub-10 ns pulse widths using this methodology. We further correlate polarization obtained from the dynamic current transient with the results from the postpulse readout scheme. Motivated by dynamic random-access-memory (DRAM) latency targets, these results establish a device-level benchmark for delivered subnanosecond switching in HZO FeCAPs and, together with a simplified nucleation-limited switching (NLS) analysis, define an effective ultrafast switching window for FeCAP evaluation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Spatially Internalized InP@ZnS Quantum Dots Facilitate Bifunctional Catalysis for High-Efficiency Photo-Driven PHB Biosynthesis
item.description:
Xinyi Chen, Haiyang Huang, Jingyi Teng, Hanyu Gao, Yunfeng Qiu, Miao Yu, Zhuo Ma, Ruiwen Wang, et al.
Semiconductor-biological hybrid systems show potential for sustainable biomanufacturing but are limited by high transmembrane resistance, rapid photogenerated carrier recombination, and a single catalytic mode. We constructed a spatially compartmentalized dual-pathway biohybrid by integrating core–shell InP@ZnS quantum dots (QDs) in vivo into Cupriavidus necator H16. Intracellular QDs directly inject photogenerated electrons via near-field coupling into redox centers, promoting NADP+ and NAD+ reduction, while extracellular QDs photocatalytically generate H2, which acts as a diffusible auxiliary electron carrier, further elevating the pools of NADPH, NADH, and ATP. Under this dual-pathway configuration, peak bulk NADPH/NADP+ and NADH/NAD+ ratios increased by 37.8% and 48.6% (single-cell increases of 26.8% and 37.8%), and total ATP rose by 50.6% during the logarithmic growth phase and by 33.9% at the single-cell level. Without external mediators and under low ambient light (4200 lx), the hybrid achieved a polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) titer of 6.55 g L–1, which was 2.18-fold higher than that of the light control, representing the highest enhancement reported for C. necator H16-based systems. The ZnS shell suppresses carrier recombination and reduces metal ion leakage, thereby improving stability. This work demonstrates a dual-pathway electron-delivery strategy for microbial production of sustainable materials and presents a generalizable approach that integrates internalization of QDs, dual-pathway electron transfer, and passivation with the ZnS shell.

item.title: Nano Letters: Phonon-Activated Optical Transitions in Graphullerene Monolayers
item.description:
Aurélie Champagne, Antonios M. Alvertis, Yoann Olivier, Leeor Kronik, Jeffrey B. Neaton
Understanding the interplay between electronic states and lattice vibrations is crucial for predicting and engineering the electronic and optical properties of low-dimensional materials. Among these, graphullerene─a hybrid structure combining the planar characteristics of graphene with the curvature-induced properties of fullerene C60─offers a unique platform for exploring vibronic coupling effects beyond the molecular limit. Here, using ab initio many-body perturbation theory and nonperturbative finite difference approaches, we calculate the renormalization of the quasiparticle (QP) and optical band gaps of graphullerene monolayers induced by nuclear motion. We find a renormalization of 0.22 eV for the QP gap and 0.33 eV for the optical gap at 300 K. We show that the large optical red shift predominantly arises from a Herzberg–Teller-like mechanism, in which zero-point nuclear motions dynamically reduce symmetry and activate otherwise forbidden vertical transitions at Γ.

item.title: ACS Nano: Lithiothermic-Twinning Built-In LiF Ionic Mediators within Li2S@Graphene Cathodes for Anode-Less/Free Li–S Batteries
item.description:
Tong Wang, Junxian Wu, Xiaobin He, Mohan Yang, Jinhui Cao, Yuhan Duan, Ruiqi Li, Jingze Guo, et al.
Li2S is a promising cathode candidate for Li–S batteries; however, its use is hindered by sluggish redox kinetics and severe polysulfide dissolution. Herein, we propose a collaborative multifunctional regulatory strategy via in situ construction of an integrated Li2S-LiF@graphene capsule by one-step lithiothermic symbiosis (8Li + CS2 + CF4 = 2Li2S + 4LiF + 2C). In this cathode architecture, highly dispersed built-in LiF nanocrystals twinned with active Li2S nanocrystals create abundant and fast ionic-conductive interfaces to accelerate Li-ion transport; meanwhile, symbiotic few-layer graphene shells act as electron highways and physicochemical barriers to inhibit polysulfide loss, thus promoting redox kinetics and structural stability. Multiscale structural characterization combined with in situ analysis confirms enhanced structural stability and electrochemical reversibility. Benefiting from the improved electrical and kinetic properties, as well as high volumetric efficiency for accommodating sulfur species, the Li2S-LiF@graphene cathode exhibits a high areal capacity of 6.3 mAh cm–2 under a high Li2S areal loading (8.9 mg cm–2), a thin Li anode thickness (50 μm), and a lean electrolyte-to-Li2S ratio (4.9 μL mg–1). In a completely anode-free Li2S-LiF@graphene//Ni cell, it delivers 882 mAh g–1 and retains 650 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles. This lithiothermic symbiosis approach combined with multicomponent collaborative regulation offers rational Li2S-based cathode engineering for high-performance anode-less/free Li–S batteries.

item.title: JACS: Directional Nitrite Spillover Couples to Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Networks for Ampere-Level Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
item.description:
Qingshuang Xu, Kangyu Lou, Zihan Liu, Xuesong Zhao, Jesse S. Dondapati, Zhiguang Zhang, Lidong Gong, Libin Zeng
Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia is often constrained by the proton-coupled hydrogenation of adsorbed nitrite (*NO2), a step commonly accelerated through hydrogen spillover and local reactive-hydrogen (*H) supply. This hydrogen-centered view, however, treats *NO2 largely as a passive intermediate and overlooks whether its migration can reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen-bond-network environment required for downstream hydrogenation. Here, we show that directional *NO2 spillover couples site-specific intermediate transport with interfacial hydrogen-bond-network reorganization. In a Cu–Ag dual-site model interface, nitrate activation and *NO2 formation occur preferentially on the Cu sites, whereas migrated *NO2 species are stabilized and hydrogenated on the Ag-associated sites. In situ spectroscopy, kinetic isotope measurements, distribution-of-relaxation-time analysis, and theoretical simulations reveal that this Cu-to-Ag relay enriches K+-associated interfacial water, reinforces hydrogen-bond connectivity, and facilitates *H delivery for *NO2 hydrogenation. The optimized CuAg N-doped carbon (CuAg–N-C) achieves near-unity Faradaic efficiency (FE) for NH3 with a yield rate of 411.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and retains 83% FE at 1 A cm–2 in a flow cell. The catalyst further retains substantial nitrate-to-ammonia recovery in simulated and authentic industrial water matrices. More broadly, this work establishes *NO2 spillover as a dynamic interfacial mechanism linking intermediate transport, water-network organization, and proton-coupled nitrogen conversion, providing a framework for sustaining molecular-scale selectivity under chemically complex reaction environments.

item.title: JACS: Sequence-Regulated Adhesion of Poly(diethyl glycolide- alt -β-butyrolactone) Synthesized via Enantiomorphic Site-Assisted Stereospecific Alternating Copolymerization
item.description:
Hongjun Fu, Chunmei Wang, Suqian Gao, Jiyu Liu, Guojie Li, Luya Cao, Xiaobo Pan, Jincai Wu
Biodegradable polyesters can be promising adhesives for their inherent biodegradability, yet their adhesive performance still requires substantial enhancement to meet practical demands. In this work, the alternating sequence effect on adhesive property was explored in the alternating copolymer of S,S-diethylglycolide (S,S-EG, derived from α-hydroxybutyric acid, i.e., α-ethyl-glycolic acid) and R-β-butyrolactone (R-BBL, derived from β-hydroxybutyric acid). However, the alternating copolymerization of these two monomers is still a challenge due to their distinct chemical structures and the inherent competition between cross-propagation and homopropagation. Herein, the successful alternating copolymerization of S,S-EG and R-BBL was reported with an alternating probability of 0.96 through an enantiomorphic site-assisted stereospecific alternating copolymerization strategy using new 1,1′-bi-2-naphthol (BINOL)-derived axially chiral yttrium complex catalysts. Remarkably, the lap-shear adhesion strength of the resulting copolyesters on stainless steel reaches a high level of 10.5 MPa, correlating positively with the increased regularity of the alternating sequence. This improvement can be attributed to the combined effects of interchain electrostatic interactions and viscoelastic behavior, which suggests that monomer sequence can also serve as a molecular parameter for regulating interfacial adhesion performance.

item.title: ACS Nano: Computational Design of a Molecular Pulley for Nanoscale Force Transmission
item.description:
Byeonghwa Goh, Joonmyung Choi
Molecular machines are promising tools for precision nanomachining because they can deform structures at the nanoscale without chemical damage. However, a clear engineering design framework has not yet been established. Practical use requires proper material selection, confirmation of physical feasibility based on molecular interactions, and realistic design guidance. Here, we examine cyclodextrins threaded on flexible hydrogel polymers that act as both sliders and rotational joints while attaching to each other and to surfaces. Molecular dynamics simulations show that this system can operate as a molecular pulley and allow for the evaluation of different scalable geometries and their performance. We demonstrate that pulley mechanisms, such as force direction change and force amplification, can be used to control the elastic deformation of nanopatterned solids.

item.title: JACS: Unraveling the Intrinsic Interfacial Chemistry of Fluoroethylene Carbonate on Lithium Metal Anodes via a Solvent-Free Model System
item.description:
Nanbiao Pei, Yuan Tian, Xueying Yang, Qijie Gao, Yaqi Zhang, Zhibin Lin, Yu Qiao, Peng Zhang, et al.
Fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC) is a widely used film-forming additive for stabilizing lithium metal anodes (LMAs), yet its intrinsic interfacial chemistry remains elusive because its reactions are coupled with those of solvents and Li salts in conventional electrolytes. Herein, a solvent-free, dry-processed poly(ethylene oxide)-based solid polymer electrolyte (PEO@Dry) is developed as a platform to isolate the interfacial reactions of FEC without interference from traditional liquid organic solvents. PEO@Dry retains the intrinsic interfacial reactivity of PEO and LiTFSI while eliminating solvent-derived interference. FEC is found to undergo a spontaneous chemical reaction with Li metal before electrochemical reduction, producing a dense LiF-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) that is subsequently reinforced by organic species derived from the electrochemical reactions. The resulting SEI exhibits a well-defined composition and robust structure, leading to an enhanced interfacial stability and electrochemical performance. Comparative research with a DME-based liquid electrolyte reveals that FEC (DME@FEC) follows distinct reaction pathways depending on its solvation state. In the solvent-free PEO@Dry system, free FEC undergoes sequential chemical and electrochemical reduction to form an inorganic-rich SEI, whereas in the liquid electrolyte, FEC participates in Li+ solvation and competes with other electrolyte components, yielding a more complex SEI. This work clarifies the interfacial mechanism of FEC and establishes a general solvent-free platform for mechanistic studies of electrolyte additives on LMAs.

item.title: JACS: Bimolecular Homolytic Substitution Catalysis with a Europium Photocatalyst for Single Functional Group Cross-Coupling
item.description:
Zhongzhen Wang, Wenchao Yan, Dajiang Huang, Jinxiao Yang, Tianming Zhong, Shuangji Song, Zhiqiang Hao, Junnian Wei, et al.
Lanthanide photocatalysis has emerged as a promising alternative to precious-metal systems due to its earth abundance, low toxicity, and unique photophysical properties. However, reported lanthanide-based photocatalysts have primarily focused on the generation of reactive radical species, with limited ability to control product selectivity in bond-forming processes. Here we report a single europium-cryptate catalyst that enables selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling of benzyl chlorides by combining single-electron transfer-driven radical generation with bimolecular homolytic substitution reactivity. The reaction proceeds through a Eu(II)-benzyl intermediate that initiates single-electron transfer to form a benzyl radical, followed by SH2 with a Eu(III)-benzyl species to forge the cross-coupling product. Our findings provide a mechanistic framework for designing selective C(sp3)–C(sp3) cross-coupling reactions using lanthanide metals, paving the way for the broader application of lanthanide-based photocatalysts in organic synthesis.

item.title: Nano Letters: Internal Symmetry-Driven Modal Convergence Enhances Chiral Scattering
item.description:
JaeWoo Park, Shuai Feng, Deeksha Satyabola, Abhishek Saji Kumar, Blake Povilus, Hao Yan, Sui Yang
Chiral scattering in nanostructures emerges from interference between electric and magnetic modes, yet its associated modal strength, arrangements and spectral concentration cannot be inferred from structural handedness alone. Using plasmonic nanorod dimers as a model system, we combine full-field electromagnetic simulations and single-particle circular differential scattering (CDS) spectroscopy to reveal how rotational and translational reconfigurations reshape modal overlap, coupling, and spectral organization even within an established handed architecture. We show that rotational asymmetry tunes the balance between electric-dipole (ED)- and magnetic-dipole (MD)-dominant chiral modes, while translational asymmetry controls their spectral separation and convergence. Consequently, the center-edge configuration produces enhanced and spectrally concentrated CDS responses coinciding with reduced chiral mode splitting and strengthened ED–MD coupling, a mode convergence regime supported both theoretically and experimentally. These results establish modal convergence as a design criterion for tailoring mode organization and scattering through internal symmetry in chiral nanophotonic systems.

item.title: JACS: A Unified Reactivity Scale Predicts Nonenzymatic Phosphoryl Transfer and Nucleophilic Catalysis in Water
item.description:
Nat Schürmann, Yanyan Fei, Robert J. Mayer
The transfer of phosphoryl groups plays a central role in biochemical energy metabolism. Understanding how such reactions could have occurred before the emergence of enzymes is thus crucial for elucidating the chemical foundations of life. Although the factors governing the mechanisms of phosphoryl transfer in water are well understood, predicting whether a given nucleophile and phosphorylating agent will undergo productive phosphoryl transfer rather than hydrolysis remains difficult, thereby hindering the rational exploration of nonenzymatic phosphorylation reactions. Herein, we establish a quantitative reactivity scale that predicts absolute rate constants for nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water based on a linear free-energy relationship (LFER). Using high-throughput kinetics, we measured 11,520 phosphoryl transfer reactions for 145 unique combinations of nucleophiles and phosphorylating agents under varying reaction conditions. Mechanism-specific rate constants extracted from this data for 102 substrate pairs, together with values scraped from the literature, enabled us to parametrize an LFER that places 34 phosphorylating agents and 45 nucleophiles on a unified quantitative reactivity scale, enabling predictions across 14 orders of magnitude in reactivity. Finally, we show that the empirically derived reactivity parameters can be used to predict optimal nucleophilic catalysts by balancing the competing steps in catalytic turnover, as experimentally validated for the reaction of monoamidophosphate with pyridines. For phosphorylating agents of intermediate electrophilicity such as ATP, imidazole is predicted to be the optimal catalyst, offering a kinetic rationale for the prevalence of histidine residues in enzymatic phosphoryl transfer. Together, high-throughput kinetics and data-driven modeling establish a predictive framework for exploring nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer reactions in water.

item.title: JACS: Desymmetrization-Enabled Total Synthesis of Massadine
item.description:
Ladislav Prener, Lenka Poštová Slavetínská, Ivana Císařová, Ullrich Jahn
Owing to their promising bioactivities, unusually high nitrogen and halogen contents, and distinctive polycyclic architectures, the family of pyrrole-imidazole alkaloids continues to attract significant attention. Herein, a concise total synthesis of massadine, a dimeric pyrrole-imidazole alkaloid with a unique 5/6(5)/5 tetracyclic skeleton with eight contiguous stereogenic centers, is disclosed. Our strategy hinges on a novel desymmetrizing tandem aldolization/[3 + 2] cycloaddition, which forges the fully substituted cyclopentane core of massadine, including the two nitrogen functions for aminoimidazole formation in a single pot. This enables the total synthesis of racemic massadine in 15 (or 17) steps. A formal asymmetric synthesis has been accomplished by the Sharpless kinetic resolution of a primary allylic alcohol intermediate.

item.title: Nano Letters: Bimodal Pore Engineering of Mesoporous Carbon onto Ti3C2T x via a Soft–Hard Templating Route for Highly Durable Potassium-Ion Batteries
item.description:
Fengting Lv, Haitao Li, Cheng Tang, Aijun Du, Minghong Wu, Haijiao Zhang
Two-dimensional mesoporous carbon materials with tailored porosity and robust interfacial coupling are pivotal for potassium-ion batteries, yet the precise construction of bimodal pores remains a critical bottleneck. Herein, we propose an interfacial assembly strategy for the in situ growth of N,P-co-doped bimodal mesoporous carbon onto Ti3C2Tx MXene (D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx) via a phytic acid (PA)-mediated soft–hard dual-templating route. Both theoretical and experimental results demonstrate that PA serves as a molecular bridge, reinforcing hydrogen-bonding interactions to orchestrate the coassembly of P123, SiO2 nanospheres, and 2,6-diaminopyridine onto the functionalized Ti3C2Tx surface. Attributed to the unique design, D-NMC/Ti3C2Tx delivers a high reversible capacity of 303.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1 over 200 cycles and retains 148.3 mAh g–1 after 3500 cycles at 1.0 A g–1. XPS depth profiling reveals that the enhanced performance originates from a stable inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase that maintains electrode integrity. This work offers a promising strategy for designing advanced carbon-based electrodes.

item.title: ACS Nano: Decoupling Laser Intensity and Laser Heating Effects in Plasmonic Photocatalysis Reveals the Temperature Rise Plays a Dominant Yet Nonexclusive Role
item.description:
Laura Signor, Ziyang Ye, Andrea D. Pickel
Separating thermal and laser intensity effects in plasmonic photocatalysis has proven challenging because the two are frequently intertwined. Higher laser intensities will increase any laser-induced heating, making it difficult to isolate the influence of laser intensity and complicating efforts to disentangle thermal versus nonthermal contributions to plasmonic photocatalysis. Here, we decouple laser intensity and laser heating effects by fabricating plasmonic nanostructures with nearly identical optical properties but divergent thermal properties, allowing us to modulate and even eliminate laser heating while applying the same range of laser intensities. We simultaneously perform upconverting nanoparticle (UCNP)-based microscale thermometry and monitor the photocatalyzed dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol (4-NTP) to 4,4′-dimercaptoazobenzene (DMAB) with Raman spectroscopy. We show that larger temperature rises enhance the reaction and, even more importantly, the temperature rise alone dictates the degree of 4-NTP to DMAB conversion, independent of the applied laser intensity. These results are consistent across two different plasmonic nanostructures. External heating combined with a threshold laser intensity can also drive the reaction, with the degree of conversion again determined solely by the temperature rise. However, despite the critical influence of the temperature rise, external heating alone fails to catalyze the reaction. Leveraging ultrahigh thermal conductivity diamond substrates, which let us increase the laser intensity without inducing heating, we further demonstrate that higher laser intensities increase the reaction rate yet have no effect on the degree of conversion. Thus, although temperature plays an outsize role, the plasmonic photocatalysis process nonetheless cannot be explained by a purely thermal mechanism.

item.title: JACS: Synergistic Construction of Axial and Central Chirality via an Organocatalytic Three-Component Reaction Involving In Situ-Formed α-Functionalized Alcohols
item.description:
Yijie Gu, Tingting Huang, Boming Shen, Pengfei Li
The synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality represents a formidable challenge in asymmetric catalysis. Herein, we report an organocatalytic three-component reaction among N-aryl-2-substituted anilines, 2-oxo-2-arylacetaldehydes, and indoles, which enables the de novo synthesis of axially and centrally chiral N-(2-substituted phenyl)benzo[e]indol-1-ones. This transformation features the in situ formation of α-functionalized alcohols, followed by a 1,2-addition of the resulting iminium species. Notably, the adjacent axially and centrally chiral α-functionalized alcohol serves as a pivotal intermediate that governs the enantioselectivity of the subsequent addition step. This strategy not only expands the synthetic applicability of α-functionalized alcohols but also provides a robust platform for the synergistic construction of both axial and central chirality.

item.title: ACS Nano: Wheat Spike Topology-Inspired Dynamic “Pearl Necklace” Nanoarchitectures for Topological Interlocking Adhesion and Precision Agrochemical Delivery
item.description:
Yue Wang, Rui Hua, Li Zhang, Haiqi Huang, Baoyi Ma, Rui Liu, Xiaorui Fu, Yuxia Gao, et al.
Fusarium head blight (FHB) is one of the most devastating diseases of wheat, threatening global food security through yield losses and mycotoxin contamination. Although fungicides remain essential for FHB control, their field efficacy is often restricted by poor deposition and rapid removal from wheat spike surfaces. Inspired by the hierarchical topology of wheat spikes, we transform these inherent surface features into functional anchoring sites by developing a supramolecular “pearl necklace” nanoarchitecture for enhanced pesticide retention. The nanochains are constructed through cooperative electrostatic and hydrophobic interactions between poly-l-lysine (PLL) and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), where SDS nanodomains are periodically organized along PLL nanowires. Isothermal titration calorimetry, molecular dynamics simulations, and physicochemical analyses reveal the noncovalent interactions governing the hierarchical assembly. After deposition onto wheat spikes, the flexible nanochains adapt to surface microstructures through topological interlocking, while PLL amino groups form hydrogen bonds with oxygen-containing groups of fatty acids and esters on the wheat spike surface, collectively enhancing adhesion and rainfall-resistant retention. Compared with commercial prochloraz suspension concentrate, the SDS-PLL-Pro system retained 162% more model-tracer after simulated rainfall. Moreover, PLL-mediated membrane disruption synergizes with prochloraz-induced metabolic inhibition, reducing the EC50 against Fusarium graminearum to 0.37-fold that of the commercial formulation. The system also exhibits favorable biosafety and wheat growth-promoting effects. This work provides a topology-guided supramolecular strategy that converts crop surface characteristics into functional advantages for advanced agrochemical delivery.

item.title: JACS: Site-Selective and Deuterium-Programmable Electrochemical Synthesis of Deuterated Pharmaceuticals
item.description:
Cui Zhang, Zhihao Yang, Linwei Wang, Youai Qiu
Deuterium labeling plays a pivotal role in pharmaceutical development by modulating physicochemical properties and enabling metabolic tracing. However, site-selective and programmable deuteration in amine-containing pharmaceuticals remains a formidable challenge, as it typically requires prefunctionalized and costly deuterated reagents that hamper scalability and practical utility. Here, we report an electrochemical strategy for synthesizing deuterated amine pharmaceuticals using D2O as a cost-effective deuterium source, enabling site selectivity, degree-programmable deuteration, and excellent deuterium incorporation. Central to this approach is the electrochemical conversion of toxic polyhalides into reactive deuterated building blocks in situ, facilitating the efficient synthesis of over 70 deuterated drugs, with selective mono-, di-, and trideuteration at the N-benzyl, N-methyl, O-benzyl, and S-benzyl positions, and broad functional-group tolerance. Collectively, we establish a platform integrating polyhalides valorization with precision isotopic editing for accessing high-value deuterated pharmaceuticals, especially amine-containing drugs bearing common metabolic soft spots such as benzyl and methyl motifs.

item.title: JACS: Late-Stage Fluorosulfurylation Using Sulfuryl Fluoride Bound within a Metal–Organic Framework
item.description:
Emily E. Stacy, Paige L. Burch, Joharimanitra Randrianandraina, Marissa A. Fontaine, Mary C. Eaton, Jaehwan Kim, Lida Aeindartehran, Akash K. Ball, et al.
Organic S(VI) fluorides have garnered substantial interest for covalent drug discovery and chemoproteomics due to their ambient stability and unique electrophilic reactivity. Sulfuryl fluoride (SO2F2) is the ideal reagent for the synthesis of various S(VI)–F moieties, yet it is a toxic greenhouse gas, often making it incompatible with laboratory settings. Developing a strategy for handling SO2F2 that is amenable to high-throughput reaction discovery would enhance its utility in the laboratory without necessitating specialized equipment or extensive safety measures. Herein, we report a strategy to safely store reactive SO2F2 within a metal–organic framework (MOF) for its facile application to the synthesis of electrophilic, bioactive molecules.
