The solid SO2F2–Mg2(dobdc) reagent can be stored for at least five months with minimal gas loss due to the strong yet reversible interaction between SO2F2 and Mg2+ centers in the MOF, as confirmed by single-crystal X-ray diffraction. Using this reagent, we prepare a range of drug-like arylfluorosulfates, primary and secondary acyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, saturated N-heterocyclic sulfamoyl fluorides, and N-heteroarene sulfamoyl fluorides, the last of which cannot be accessed using sulfonium salt alternatives to SO2F2 due to the requirement for strongly basic conditions. These findings represent the first experimental study of SO2F2 adsorption within a MOF and the first use of MOFs for late-stage fluorosulfurylation, paving the way toward a general approach to carefully handling dangerous, reactive gases as solid reagents.

item.title: ACS Nano: Correlating Defects and Surface Contaminants: Toward Clean Graphene with Improved Mechanical Performance
item.description:
Ziqi Wang, Shize Feng, Huy Q. Ta, Xiaoting Liu, Liming Zheng, Fan Xia, Zhiping Xu, Zhong Zhang, et al.
The mechanical performance of large-area chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene membranes is often compromised by coexisting lattice defects and surface contamination. However, the underlying synergistic mechanisms remain elusive, particularly regarding how defects mediate contaminant nucleation and how their coupling degrades the mechanical properties of graphene. Here, combining in situ spherical aberration-corrected transmission electron microscopy with controlled contaminant removal and redeposition experiments, we provide atomic-scale experimental validation for the causal correlation between graphene point defects and amorphous carbon contamination on CVD-grown graphene. We further achieve real-time, site-resolved visualization of active carbon species migration and defect-trapping dynamics. Multiscale simulations uncover a defect-mediated kinetic-trapping mechanism: active carbon species migrate rapidly over intact graphene yet become captured and immobilized at defects, with the calculated diffusion coefficient dropping from ∼14.4 to 1.65 nm2 ns–1. Moreover, nanoindentation tests confirm that clean graphene exhibits superior mechanical properties (stiffness: ∼305 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1900 nN) compared to the contaminated counterpart (stiffness: ∼224 N m–1 and fracture force: ∼1077 nN). Continuum finite-element analysis indicates that the reduced stiffness of unclean graphene cannot be explained by surface contamination alone, supporting the presence of defect-induced softening beneath the contamination. Atomically resolved simulations further reveal that the mechanical response is jointly governed by defect type, contamination, and interfacial bonding. In particular, chemically bonded contamination can redistribute local stress and mitigate defect-induced stress concentration, thereby altering the failure process of defective graphene. Our study identifies point defects as both contamination traps and mechanical weak links, offering a unified strategy for high-performance graphene membrane design.

item.title: Nano Letters: Photoluminescence as a Quantitative Probe of Semiconductor Nanocrystals
item.description:
Leo Luber, Luca Reim, Daphne Benedikt, Andreas Singldinger, Alexander S. Urban
Photoluminescence spectroscopy is among the most established characterization techniques for semiconductor nanocrystals, yet routine analysis is often limited to the emission peak position and full width at half-maximum. Here, we identify a common statistical structure in ensemble photoluminescence and introduce a Gaussian asymmetric Laplace (GaLa) framework that transforms this structure into quantitative information about the emissive ensemble. The model describes emission as the convolution of a Gaussian contribution with independent low- and high-energy spectral tails. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal distinct thermal evolution of these contributions, while the same statistical form captures diverse nanocrystal compositions, morphologies, and environments. Where an appropriate size–energy relationship is available, the Gaussian width can be mapped onto relative size dispersion, while systematic deviations expose hidden emissive subpopulations. Applied during CsPbBr3 nanocube syntheses, GaLa analysis simultaneously tracks nanocrystal growth and ensemble focusing, establishing routine photoluminescence as a quantitative probe of nanocrystal ensembles.

item.title: ACS Nano: Plasmonic Hot Carrier-Driven Chemistry Revealed by Dual Raman Thermometry
item.description:
Shengxiang Wu, Sa Suo, Nandan Ghorai, Isaac Tangen, Jinhui Meng, Tianquan Lian
Plasmonic nanoparticles (NPs) have been employed as nanocatalysts in a myriad of photochemical reactions with the underlying mechanisms divided into two categories: thermal and nonthermal pathways. Differentiating these two pathways is the key to optimizing plasmon-mediated chemistry; however, the challenge of measuring temperature down to the nanoscale hinders the advancement and causes the ongoing debate in the field. Herein, we report an in situ spectroscopic approach that leverages two Raman thermometries─the background of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (plasmonic thermometry) and molecular vibrational fingerprints (molecular thermometry) are used independently to probe the local temperature of NP/molecule hybrid systems. Using gold NP/4-nitrothiophenol as a prototype system, we demonstrate the agreement between the two thermometries and prove the nonthermal pathways for the dimerization of 4-nitrothiophenol. Since the temperatures of both metal NPs and adsorbed molecules are probed simultaneously, the dual Raman thermometry enables a detailed mechanistic understanding of plasmon-mediated chemistry.

item.title: ACS Nano: Regime of Geometrical Mismatch in the Phase Separation-Regulated Endocytosis of Nanoparticles
item.description:
Xueqing Jin, Zheng Jiao, Jiaqi Li, Jingzhe Wang, Li-Tang Yan
The biological responses related to microdomains formed by phase separation in cell membranes bear long-standing controversies, and, in particular, how this lateral heterogeneity impacts the cellular uptake of nanoparticles remains poorly understood. By combining theoretical models, computer simulations, and experimental discussions, we report on an unconventionally constrained regime of nanoparticle endocytosis on the membrane microdomain, emerging within the intermediate scale of the domains. This regime leads to the nonmonotonic dependence of nanoparticle endocytosis on domain size, in stark contrast to its counterparts in the homogeneous membrane and endocytosis without nanoparticles. Theoretical analysis evaluates the regime boundary and reveals that the regime arises from the geometrical mismatch between nanoparticles and microdomains governed by various energetic contributions, which capture and explain some experimental observations. The findings suggest an appealing way and useful guidelines to control cellular uptake and might be of immediate interest to the desired biomedical applications.

item.title: Nano Letters: Accelerated Oxygen Redox Kinetics via Synergistic Electron Modulation at Asymmetric Dual 180° Oxygen Bonds in Co-Free Li-Rich Cathodes
item.description:
Yan Liu, Zewen Liu, Zhen Wu, Meiqi Wang, Jiadong Liang, Peifan Qu, Jilu Zhang, Qin Wang, et al.
While oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes enables exceptionally high capacities, its sluggish kinetics often lead to poor rate capability and severe voltage decay. Here, we construct asymmetric, near-180° Li–O–Al and Li–O–Na configurations that target the oxygen states in a Co-free, Mn-rich cathode. We demonstrate that Li–O–Al configuration lowers the energy barrier for oxygen electron excitation through strong Al–O covalency, whereas the Li–O–Na structure enhances the electron-loss capability of active oxygen. The interplay between these two configurations improves the kinetics of the oxygen redox reaction. This modulation effectively accelerates both electronic and ionic transport in lithium-rich materials during high-voltage cycling. The Al/Na codoped cathode delivers 314.8 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and 151.2 mAh g–1 at 5 C, compared with 222.6 and 85.8 mAh g–1 for the undoped cathode. This dual-configuration strategy enables high-capacity and accelerated oxygen redox in Mn-rich, Co-free, and Li-rich cathodes.

item.title: ACS Nano: Ferroelectric Neuromorphic Devices Enable Nonphotosensitive Neurons to Achieve Event-Driven Photosensitive Artificial Neural Interfaces
item.description:
Feng Guo, Di Zhao, Weng Fu Io, Yong Wu, Lei Sun, Guoling Feng, Zhaoying Dang, Yunan Lin, et al.
Neuromorphic devices integrated with biological neurons hold significant potential for rehabilitation and human-machine interfaces, thereby attracting extensive research interest. However, the effort to connect them through light stimulation is still in its very initial stages. Here, ferroelectric neuromorphic devices based on α-In2Se3 and P(VDF-TrFE) are proposed to construct hybrid neural interfaces. In contrast to neuromorphic devices employing other working principles, ferroelectricity plays a crucial role in connecting biological neurons, which enables nonphotosensitive neurons to respond to light stimuli. Various optoelectronic synaptic behaviors have been achieved. Under light pulses, the ferroelectric neuromorphic device induced a significant increase of up to 200% in the calcium ion signal of artificial neural interfaces. Patch-clamp was applied for further verification, revealing the influence of different light wavelengths and pulse frequencies on neuronal excitation signals, which is analogous to the human retina. Simulations demonstrate that the ferroelectric neural interface improves dynamic gesture recognition accuracy from 51% to 99%. Our approach offers a strategy to connect neuromorphic devices with neurons through light, which may offer a platform to investigate the fundamental principles of synaptic plasticity and learning in a hybrid setting for future remote therapy and human–machine interfaces.

item.title: ACS Nano: Interphase-Adaptive Chloride Solid Electrolyte Enables High-Performance All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
item.description:
Huan Hu, Zhixuan Yu, Long Xie, Tengxiao Mu, Zhaoyu Rong, Zhihao Yan, Jiangtao Wang, XuanYu Lou, et al.
Halide solid electrolytes offer a compelling combination of wide electrochemical stability and high safety for all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs), yet their practical application is severely hindered by interfacial degradation, mechanical contact loss, and low active-material utilization when paired with Ni-rich layered oxide cathodes. Here we synthesize a monoclinic Li2.4Yb0.4Zr0.6Cl6 (LYZC) with a high ionic conductivity of 2.1 × 10–3 S·cm–1 at 30 °C, and then coat it with an ultrathin amorphous organic interphase (LYZC@CH) through an organic-solvent-assisted low-temperature strategy. The adaptive organic interphase transforms the intrinsically rigid chloride electrolyte into a chemo-mechanically compliant ion conductor that accommodates cathode volume variation while preserving rapid lithium–ion transport. Consequently, the engineered electrolyte stabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interface, suppresses parasitic interfacial reactions and structural degradation, and enables composite cathodes with a high active-material content of 90%. The resulting LiNi0.83Co0.12Mn0.05O2 composite cathode delivers an electrode-level energy density of 402.22 Wh kg–1 and retains nearly 100% of its capacity after 2000 cycles at 5 C in 30 MPa. This work establishes an electrolyte-centered interfacial engineering strategy for practical high-energy all-solid-state lithium batteries.

item.title: ACS Nano: Microalgae-Macrophage Hybrid Exosome-like Nanovesicles for Mitophagy Restoration and Wound Regeneration in Aging
item.description:
Boya Cheng, Donghu Lin, Ziwei Wang, Yutong Lang, Yangyang Hu, Wentao Liu, Siyan Liu, Jia Dong, et al.
The wound healing capacity in the elderly is significantly impaired, leading to increased susceptibility to inflammation and infection, and potentially contributing to reduced lifespan. In aged wounds, dysfunctional mitophagy in senescent cells (SnCs) results in the persistent release of pro-inflammatory cytokines, fostering a chronic inflammatory microenvironment that further delays tissue repair. To address this challenge, we developed a thermosensitive hydrogel loaded with hybrid exosome-like nanovesicles to enhance wound healing in aging. These hybrid nanovesicles (termed SP-M2-ENs) were generated by extrusion-mediated fusion of spirulina-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (SP-ENs) with M2 macrophage-derived exosome-like nanovesicles (M2-ENs). SP-ENs are rich in phycocyanin and exhibit strong antioxidant activity, whereas M2-ENs carry multiple anti-inflammatory cytokines and growth factors. This synergistic combination endows the hybrid system with enhanced anti-inflammatory and regenerative capabilities. To ensure sustained release and conformability to irregular wound topographies, the hybrid nanovesicles were encapsulated within a thermosensitive hydrogel (PF-127 gel), forming the final therapeutic construct, designated SP-M2-ENs@Gel. Comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that SP-M2-ENs@Gel effectively scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS), promotes tissue regeneration, stimulates angiogenesis, modulates macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype, and enables prolonged delivery of therapeutic agents. Specifically, SP-M2-ENs@Gel accelerates healing in aged wounds by restoring mitophagy function in senescent cells, thereby alleviating chronic inflammation. Collectively, this platform represents a promising strategy for overcoming senescence-impaired wound repair, highlighting the clinical translatability of engineered exosome-based therapies in regenerative medicine.

item.title: Nano Letters: Dark Exciton Signatures in the Infrared Transient Absorption of MoS2 Monolayer
item.description:
Tian-Xiang Qian, Marco D’Alessandro, Claudio Attaccalite, Tian-Yi Cai, Sheng Ju, Davide Sangalli
Dark excitons play a central role in the nonequilibrium dynamics of two-dimensional semiconductors but remain difficult to characterize. Interexciton transient absorption (exc-tr-abs) in experiments, with probes tuned in the exciton–exciton transitions energy range, can detect excitations from any populated dark excitons, including symmetry-forbidden, spin-forbidden, and finite-momentum ones. In this work, we develop a GW+BSE scheme for computing exc-tr-abs spectra from arbitrary populated exciton distributions. These dark excitons are included equally by evaluating exciton–exciton dipoles in a locally smooth gauge, including intra- and interband contributions. For monolayer MoS2, the exc-tr-abs signal arises from the Γ, K, M, and Q valleys, differing substantially from the Γ-only interpretation. Exciton–exciton dipoles show similar intensities across these valleys, while their weights are dictated by initial excitonic populations. State- and spin-resolved analyses assign the peaks to 1s → 2p and 1s → 3p transitions from both spin-flip and spin-conserving A and B excitons across valleys and momenta.

item.title: JACS: Overturning the Thermal Instability Paradigm of Ether-Based Electrolytes via Multi-Anion-Driven Solvation Reconstruction
item.description:
Xinhui Zeng, Jian Chen, Xu Xu, Xiaoyan Shi, Xiaosa Zhang, Yun Wan, Haoyu Si, Yixuan Zhang, et al.
Ether-based electrolytes have attracted considerable attention due to their excellent ion-transport kinetics and favorable interfacial compatibility with hard carbon anodes. However, their poor thermal stability severely limits the long-term stable operation of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) under high-temperature operating conditions. Herein, a multi-anion ether-based electrolyte is proposed to concurrently boost the high-temperature tolerance and fast-charging performance of SIBs by regulating solvation structures and enriching electrolyte molecular diversity. The introduction of FSI– and TFSI– anions not only favors the formation of an anion-reinforced solvation microenvironment but also substantially diminishes the size of ionic clusters. The anion-reinforced solvation structure lowers the desolvation energy barrier and promotes the formation of robust, inorganic-rich electrode–electrolyte interphases, which significantly improves high-temperature stability. Meanwhile, the smaller ionic clusters facilitate higher ionic conductivity and homogeneous Na+ flux distribution, thereby effectively suppressing sodium plating under fast-charging conditions. As a result, the Prussian blue||hard carbon full cell delivers superior rate performance and cycling stability at a wide temperature range of 10–100 °C. In addition, Ah-level pouch cells exhibit stable cycling at 55 °C with a reversible capacity of 1023.58 mAh after 800 cycles (80.8% retention) and deliver a high discharge capacity of 1008.99 mAh at 2.0 C.

item.title: JACS: Inverse Design of Inorganic Compounds with Generative AI
item.description:
Hannes Kneiding, Lucía Morán-González, Nishamol Kuriakose, Ainara Nova, David Balcells
Machine learning is revolutionizing chemistry. Beyond the value of predictive models accelerating virtual screening, generative AI aims at enabling inverse design, reversing the compound-to-property prediction paradigm into property-to-compound generation. Chemists now have access to a rich AI toolbox for organic chemistry, including drug discovery. However, the application of these methods to inorganic compounds remains limited by the challenges posed by their intrinsic nature. This perspective analyzes how these challenges have been addressed, considering widely diverse systems ranging from molecules to crystals, including transition metal complexes and microporous materials. The analysis focuses on how generative AI methods have evolved toward data-representation-model pipelines that address the full complexity of inorganic compounds, including their chemical composition, geometry, symmetry, and electronic structure. Future directions, like benchmark standardization and the development of synthesizability metrics, are also discussed.

item.title: Nano Letters: In Situ Growth of Polyanionic DNA Hydrogel Networks for Nanoconfined Iontronic Analysis of DNA Methylation
item.description:
Bingheng Li, Zimeng Zhang, Yalei Gao, Bing Bo, Jian Ni, Liu Shi, Liang Mao
Solid-state nanofluidics offers unique ion transport dynamics for sensitive molecular diagnostics. Herein, we report a nanoconfined iontronic platform for quantifying trace p16 gene methylation (p16-mC) in liquid biopsies. This system couples sequence-specific hybridization with HpaII enzymatic cleavage to strictly eliminate false positives from unmethylated homologues. Genuine target recognition triggers interfacial rolling circle and multiple-primer chain amplifications directly at anodic aluminum oxide nanochannel orifices. This in situ topological growth yields a 3D polyanionic DNA hydrogel that fundamentally remodels the interfacial physicochemical microenvironment. The resulting superhydrophilic transition and localized surface charge accumulation synergistically amplify transmembrane cation conductance, translating subtle epigenetic variations into robust iontronic readouts. Driven by this physical gating, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of ∼33 aM and a dynamic range spanning 10 orders of magnitude. Clinically, the platform effectively discriminates nonsmall cell lung cancer patients from healthy donors using peripheral plasma, demonstrating its clinical feasibility for noninvasive cancer diagnostics.

item.title: JACS: Spiral-in-Shrink Assembly of Microarchitected Circularly Polarized Luminescent Networks
item.description:
Tingjie Lv, Qi Guo, Guangen Li, Zeyi Li, Yanji Huang, Yajie Zhou, Shanshan Zhao, Mingjiang Zhang, et al.
High-fidelity three-dimensional displays require precise control over the polarization of light. Screens incorporating chiral emissive micropixels─which allow effective regulation of spin angular momentum─offer the potential for minimal-crosstalk, high-definition imaging. However, such highly asymmetric luminous, densely integrated microarrays have not yet been reported, owing to interfacial pinning effects and easy chiral structural degradation during miniaturization. Here, we present a spiral-in-shrink assembly strategy that couples evaporation-induced contraction with chiral self-organization in a nonequilibrium pathway. Geometry-confined shrinkage and chiral helically ordered microdomes act in concert to stabilize circularly polarized emission, yielding lateral features of 58 μm─corresponding to a significant improvement in miniaturization over reported dimensions. Large-area arrays comprising over 31,000 emissive units achieve 359 pixels per inch─and luminescence dissymmetry factors up to 1.25, enabling densely packed full-color photonic patterning. Moreover, spatially encoded handedness distributions underpin polarization-resolved mapping on aerial platforms for human–machine sensing. Our scalable route establishes a platform for cohesive chiroptical materials across advanced optical displays, polarization imaging, and intelligent sensing.

item.title: ACS Nano: Electron-Modulated Pt–Co Dual-Atom Sites with Hydrogen Spillover for Robust Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
Xiaoxiao Wu, Yuguang Wang, Rui Wan, Jing Zhang, He Liu, Bin Chen, Guowen Meng
Pt single-atom catalysts (Pt-SACs) are regarded as one of the most promising electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) owing to the maximal atom utilization and distinctive coordination structure. However, their reaction kinetics and stability at large current density are severely limited by the linear scaling relations and metal sites agglomeration. Herein, we present an “electronic anchoring strategy” to construct Pt–Co dual-atom sites (PtCo-DASs) on onion-like carbon nanospheres with carbon vacancies (OLCv) (denoted PtCo-DAS@OLCv) as a structurally integrated electrode for highly efficient and stable HER. Experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate that Pt atoms achieve electron capture through d–π orbital coupling with Co, C, and O, subsequently guarantee superior structural stability, and establish a localized electric field. The electric field is further amplified by the confinement effect from the high-curvature of nanosized OLCv, which facilitates proton enrichment, lowers the Volmer barrier, and accelerates hydrogen spillover from Pt sites to Co sites, ultimately decoupling hydrogen adsorption and desorption at the atom scale. Consequently, PtCo-DAS@OLCv with an ultralow Pt loading of 6.16 μg cm–2 exhibits a high HER activity with a low overpotential of 14.1 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and high turnover frequency of 83.2 H2 s–1 at 100 mV, which are superior to those of commercial Pt/C and the most reported Pt-based catalysts. Interestingly, a practical proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer (PEMWE) assembled by PtCo-DAS@OLCv achieves a large current density of 1000 mA cm–2 at an ultralow cell voltage of 1.78 V and operates stably for over 2300 h with negligible degradation.

item.title: JACS: Functional Cooperation between Pt Single Atoms and Nanoparticles on TiO 2 for Photocatalytic Dehydrogenation and C–C Coupling
item.description:
Yuxiao Jiang, Hao Wang, Yangwei Zhang, Shirui Cui, Hongxi Wu, Jiong Li, Zelong Li, Can Li
Dehydrogenative coupling reactions that activate inert C–H bonds for C–C bond formation remain challenging because of unfavorable thermodynamics and kinetics without external oxidants. We report a hybrid photocatalytic system consisting of mixed Pt species on TiO2 (Ptmix/TiO2) combined with the hydrogen atom transfer reagent 2,2,2-trichloroethanol (TCE) for the dehydrogenative coupling of toluene. The system delivers 11% toluene conversion with 94% selectivity to bibenzyl and stoichiometric H2 evolution. Mechanistic studies show that Pt single atoms (Pt1) act as hole acceptors, while Pt nanoparticles (Pt NPs) act as electron acceptors, which further enhances charge separation. Holes localized on Pt1 oxidize TCE to generate chlorine radicals that mediate benzylic C–H abstraction, and electrons accumulated on Pt NPs drive proton reduction to H2. This work highlights the synergy between a semiconductor photocatalyst and a HAT (hydrogen atom transfer) mediator and the complementary roles of distinct Pt configurations, offering a guiding principle for designing efficient photocatalytic systems for organic synthesis.

item.title: JACS: Iron-Catalyzed Asymmetric Amino-Pyrazolation of Vinylarenes
item.description:
Xin Xu, Hui Xu, Zhan-Lin Wang, Shu-Ya Xin, Zhenbo Mo, Yanfeng Dang, Fei Wang
Stereoselective pyrazole N-alkylation has emerged as a highly sought-after transformation in both synthetic and medicinal chemistry. Despite substantial advances, existing methods have relied on two-component coupling strategies that require tailored alkylating reagents and/or noble transition metal catalysts. Herein, we report an iron-catalyzed asymmetric olefin difunctionalization platform that enables the simultaneous incorporation of both primary amino and pyrazole groups. The resulting β-primary amino pyrazoles serve as versatile synthetic linchpins that are amenable to diverse postfunctionalization reactions, thereby substantially expanding the accessible chemical space of enantioenriched N-alkyl pyrazoles. The synthetic utility of this method is further demonstrated by the streamlined synthesis of a bioactive molecule and its structural analogues. Preliminary mechanistic investigations suggest that the reaction proceeds through an enantioselective aziridination and ring-opening pyrazolation sequence.

item.title: ACS Nano: Nondestructive Piezoelectric Nanocomposite Sonodynamic Toothbrush for Synergistic Dental Disinfection and Whitening
item.description:
Jiachuan Hua, Meijin Liu, Mingxing Peng, Mingzhe Nie, Xuemin Du
Over 3.47 billion people worldwide suffer from dental health and aesthetic issues, however, existing commercial toothbrushes lack synergistic antibacterial and whitening functions and fail to prevent biofilm accumulation and progressive staining. Here, we develop novel sonodynamic bifunctional piezoelectric nanocomposites by integrating piezoelectric Au@BTO nanoparticles into a porous elastomer matrix, enabling synergistic disinfection and whitening in a biosafe and efficient manner during daily toothbrushing. These nanocomposites exhibit superior mechanical and piezoelectric stability under continuous ultrasound stimulation for 30,000 s, along with robust andcontrollable generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) based on a piezocatalytic mechanism. Under physiological conditions, the piezoelectric nanocomposites demonstrate highly efficient and durable antibacterial activity against Gram-positive S. aureus and S. mutans as well as Gram-negative E. coli and P. gingivalis (>99% efficacy), while preserving >95% oral cell viability. When integrated into an innovative Piezo-brush, the system maintains structural integrity for ∼5 months under daily toothbrushing and achieves 96% biofilm reduction and nondestructive whitening (CIELab color difference = 70.3, 0.6% Vickers hardness reduction), significantly outperforming existing functional toothbrushes and commercial products. This work develops a piezoelectric sonodynamic toothbrush for daily dental care, offering avenues for advanced biodevices in cosmetics, wound healing, and medical implants.

item.title: Nano Letters: Interfacial Kinetic Gating Mechanism via Controllable SEI Regulation toward Robust Zinc Anodes
item.description:
Qianqian Yao, Fuhao Qi, Yahui Wang, Jun Mei, Shixue Dou
Interphase chemistry is conventionally ascribed to electrolyte composition, while electrochemical operating conditions are treated merely as kinetic parameters. Here, we demonstrate applied current programs at the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) on Zn via an electrochemical kinetic-gating mechanism. N-Hydroxyethyliminodiacetic acid reorganizes Zn2+ solvation and supplies interfacial precursors, whereas current density selects their reaction pathways. High current establishes a kinetically constrained window that promotes coupled conversion of sulfate and NHA species into a compact organic–inorganic SEI enriched in ZnS and Zn–N; low-current formation produces a loose and nonprotective interphase. High-current activation enables stable Zn deposition even after switching to low current, evidencing that interphase properties are determined by formation history. The programmed anode delivers 5300 h at 5 mA cm–2, and Zn||NH4V4O10 pouch cells sustain 700 cycles. These findings establish current as an active control variable for interfacial reaction selection, offering a route toward programmable interphase chemistry beyond composition-only design.

item.title: ACS Nano: Covalent Interface-Engineered Bone-Targeting Piezoelectric Heterojunction Reprograms Tumor Stress Adaptation and Reverses the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment
item.description:
Jie Wang, Guangting Zhu, Yunxiang Ding, Ming Lei, Xuan Yan, Qingjian Lei, Sang Hu, Lin Cai, et al.
Breast cancer bone metastasis remains a major therapeutic challenge due to endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS)-associated stress adaptation and an immunosuppressive tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Herein, we report a zoledronic acid (ZOL)-loaded bone-targeted covalent piezoelectric heterojunction nanoplatform (Z@BT-P) for sonopiezo-dynamic therapy (SPDT) and immune remodeling. In this platform, barium titanate (BTO) was covalently integrated with a porphyrinic porous coordination network to form a stable BT-P heterointerface, while ZOL enhanced bone-metastatic lesion enrichment. Compared with physically assembled BT@P, Z@BT-P promoted interfacial charge utilization and strengthened ultrasound (US)-triggered piezoelectric catalysis. Under US irradiation, enhanced charge utilization and Piezo1-associated mechanosensitive Ca2+ signaling jointly amplified reactive oxygen species accumulation and Ca2+ dysregulation, causing dual oxidative/Ca2+ stress. This stress cascade promoted ERS associated with glucose-regulated protein 78 and C/EBP homologous protein, leading to apoptosis and immunogenic cell death. Consequent damage-associated molecular patterns release and ZOL-containing treatment enhanced dendritic cell maturation, drove M1-like macrophage remodeling, and activated antitumor immunity. In a 4T1-luc tibial bone metastasis model, Z@BT-P + US achieved 89.4% ± 4.9% tumor growth inhibition, alleviated osteolytic bone destruction, suppressed distant metastasis, and promoted immune memory. This study establishes a covalent interface-engineered piezoelectric nanoplatform for bone metastasis therapy.

item.title: JACS: Operando pH Measurements of OER within a Porous Oxygen-Evolving Electrode
item.description:
Zhifei Yan, Daniel M. Loh, Rui Sun, Daniel G. Nocera
Three-dimensional porous electrodes, such as those in membrane electrode assemblies, are widely employed in electrochemical devices due to their high surface area and achievable current density. The heterogeneous internal structure of the porous electrode microenvironment engenders local concentration gradients owing to mass transport constraints. Localized microenvironments with properties distinct from those of the bulk solution are especially prevalent for electrocatalytic reactions that produce or consume protons, as local basic or acidic environments may significantly influence the energy efficiency and selectivity of proton-coupled electron transfer reactions that are necessary for small-molecule activation. Here, we develop an operando method employing polymer-bound fluorescent sensors (PFS) to directly quantify local pH and the internal proton gradient in a porous electrode for the oxygen evolution reaction catalyzed by IrOx supported on indium-tin oxide (ITO). The PFS uncovers notable pH gradients within a 3-μm-thick layer of the OER electrode in unbuffered electrolyte, even at low current density. Proton transport dynamics were found to be influenced significantly by the proton adsorption properties of the ITO support, revealing a previously unrecognized role of the oxide support in modifying the local pH gradient. The PFS method should prove useful in the study and evaluation of electrochemical devices, including fuel cells, bipolar and other ion-conducting membranes, and electrolyzers.

item.title: ACS Nano: Sulfur Doping-Induced Surface Reconstruction of High-Entropy Composites Boosts Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis for Zinc-Air Batteries
item.description:
Junjie Hu, Xiongwei Zhong, Leyi Gao, Zhitong Li, Gaole Liu, Shuyu Cui, Kelin Chen, Xiaoyi Fu, et al.
The development of high-efficiency and durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for both the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is essential for the widespread application of rechargeable zinc-air batteries (RZABs). Rational screening of ORR/OER components and precise regulation of their electronic structures to achieve synergistic effects currently stand as an effective solution. Here, we report a composite catalyst prepared through the high-temperature decomposition of molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), synthesizing sulfur (S)-doped high-entropy alloy (HEA) nanoparticles on carbon nanotube (S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT) with metallic single atoms. High-valent Mo can precisely modulate the local electronic domains of HEAs. S doping not only triggers surface reconstruction of HEAs during the OER to deliver outstanding OER catalytic activity but also immobilizes metal single atoms to boost ORR: an overpotential as low as 247 mV at 10 mA cm–2 and an ORR half-wave potential of 0.746 V are achieved. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the S-doping-induced surface reconstruction promotes the adsorption of *OOH intermediates and reduces the Gibbs free energy barrier during the OER process. RZAB based on S-FeCoNiMnMo@CNT exhibits a peak power density of 229.8 mW cm–2, along with a low voltage gap of 0.716 V at 10 mA cm–2 and a cycle life exceeding 800 h. Furthermore, this work extends its applications to flexible ZABs.

item.title: JACS: From Sintering to Mineralization: A Liquid-Phase Growth Route for Ceramic Films
item.description:
Qiuxia Feng, Xinjing Zhang, Zhongwei Cao, Hongbo Li, Xuefeng Zhu, Weishen Yang
The fabrication of dense ceramic films for solid-state electronics and energy-conversion systems has long been hindered by a fundamental sintering dilemma: the high temperatures required to activate solid-state diffusion simultaneously promote elemental volatilization, interfacial reactions, and phase segregation. Inspired by natural mineralization, we develop a biomimetic liquid-phase growth (LPG) strategy that enables the direct formation of dense ceramic films under mild conditions. As a stringent model system, we select the highly refractory proton conductor BaZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ (BZY), which possesses a melting point of 2700 °C. In the LPG process, molten Ba(NO3)2 serves as both a reactive precursor and a liquid transport medium, while a (ZrO2)0.92(Y2O3)0.08 (YSZ) seed layer confines nucleation and directs interfacial crystal growth and coalescence. This strategy produces dense, chemically homogeneous BZY films at 600 °C, more than 1000 °C below those required in conventional solid-state sintering. The evolution mechanism of the LPG process is elucidated through in situ real-time characterizations. The versatility of this strategy is further demonstrated by the successful growth of BaHfO3, BaHfO3@BZY heterostructured, and SrZr0.85Y0.15O3−δ films. Fuel-cell tests validate the electrochemical functionality of the BZY-LPG electrolytes. By reconceptualizing film densification as a liquid-phase mineralization process, LPG establishes a distinct chemical framework for the low-temperature synthesis of dense films, substantially expanding the design landscape for advanced ceramic devices.

item.title: JACS: Spin Exchange Enables Two-Electron TEMPO Catholytes for Aqueous Organic Flow Batteries
item.description:
Xu Liu, Zhikun Xu, Xuri Zhang, Junjie Huang, Chi Han, Muyang Chen, Chuhao Yang, Haiyang Wu, et al.
High-energy-density neutral aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) require a transition from one-electron/one-electron and two-electron/one-electron configurations to fully two-electron-matched systems. This goal has remained unrealized because stable two-electron catholytes are lacking, and even the most promising TEMPO materials still undergo proton-induced irreversible piperidine ring opening, causing rapid capacity decay. Here we report a hydration-cage-induced spin-exchange strategy for stabilizing two-electron AcNH-NMe-TEMPO catholytes. In aqueous solution, a dynamic hydration cage preorganizes the diradical into a folded conformation, shortens the ·O–O· distance, and enables intramolecular spin exchange. In situ electron paramagnetic resonance directly captures quintet signatures of appropriate spin-exchange interactions, which reduces the possibility of triggering external interactions between TEMPO and protons, presenting a new mechanism to stabilize two-electron AORFB operation. The polarization scattering experiments confirm that increasing the spin exchange interaction can decrease the external interaction of TEMPO with the polarized environment, as shown by the reduced scattering of incident polarized photons. Crucially, mass spectrometry tracks radical evolution under proton capture, showing self-regulated stabilization of the piperidine framework. Consequently, the constructed two-electron/one-electron system exhibits exceptional durability, with 99.28% capacity retention at 3 M e–. Further developing a first two-electron/two-electron neutral all-organic system achieves a 1.4–1.7-fold increase in practical energy density relative to the two-electron/one-electron system, corresponding to a 26.1–42.3% reduction in electrolyte demand. The AcNH-NMe-TEMPO/dex-NDI system maintains 98.45% retention over 1200 cycles at 2 M e–. These results establish spin exchange as a molecular design concept for advancing high-density and long-lifetime AORFBs.

item.title: ACS Nano: Voltage-Gated Ionic Conductivity in Ultranarrow Confinement
item.description:
Sebastian Ostoja-Petkowski, Ming Chen, Alexei A. Kornyshev
Voltage-controlled ion transport in subnanometer pores underpins the operation of emerging filtration, energy-storage, and iontronic technologies, yet its microscopic mechanisms remain poorly understood. Using classical molecular dynamics simulations, we investigate ionic transport in ultranarrow (≤1 nm) quasi-two-dimensional nanopores in MXene electrodes filled with an ionic liquid. We reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of linear-response conductivity on electrode potential, with a pronounced asymmetry between positive and negative electrode polarizations. These behaviors originate from a competition between confinement-induced ionic ordering and charging-induced ion crowding within the pore. The resulting transition from a structure-limited to an ion-crowding-limited transport regime provides a general framework for understanding voltage-gated ionic conduction under extreme confinement, which facilitates the formulation of design principles for MXene-based nanofluidic, electrochemical, and iontronic devices.

item.title: ACS Nano: Quantifying Viscoelastic Alterations in Virus-Infected Cells by Optical Tweezers
item.description:
Da-Di Xu, Yawen Zheng, Liu Liu, Yu-Yao Li, Pengfei Xu, Yang Liu, Dai-Wen Pang, Hong-Wu Tang
The viscoelasticity of cells is closely related to their physiological functions, influencing processes such as differentiation, proliferation, and migration. Viruses replicate by infecting host cells and can affect the cells’ viscoelastic properties. However, current research mainly focuses on changes in the overall cellular viscoelasticity, while intracellular viscoelastic properties remain difficult to measure. Optical tweezers, due to their noncontact nature, offer a promising tool for measuring intracellular viscoelasticity. In this study, the viscoelastic moduli of host cells infected with three different viruses (H9N2, PRV, and HSV) were measured using the active-passive calibration method and microrheological techniques. The changes in viscoelastic moduli across different frequency ranges were systematically analyzed. The results showed that viral infection altered the viscoelastic properties of cells, with the extent of changes varying by virus type. We conclude that viral infection leads to an increase in viscous modulus and a decrease in elastic modulus of the host cell, and this is attributed to virus-induced depolymerization of the cytoskeleton, which reduces cellular elasticity and increases viscosity. These findings provide insights into the mechanisms of virus-induced alterations in cellular viscoelasticity and offer a theoretical foundation for further studies on the cellular mechanisms of viral infections.

item.title: JACS: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ion-Association Design Decouples Linearity and Dynamic Range in Organic Electrochemical Synapses
item.description:
Donghwa Lee, Myeongjin An, Junho Sung, Yoohyeon Jang, Hyoik Jang, Geun Yeol Bae, Eunho Lee
Organic electrochemical synaptic transistors (OESTs) are promising neuromorphic devices, but simultaneously achieving highly linear analog weight updates and a wide dynamic range remains fundamentally limited by a severe trade-off in uncontrolled interface doping kinetics. Although multicomponent electrolytes offer a pathway to tune ion behavior, a predictive framework capable of overcoming this strict trade-off remains unexplored due to the highly nonlinear nature of interionic interactions. Here, we introduce an AI-assisted ion-association design strategy utilizing a binary electrolyte architecture to break through the linearity–dynamic range trade-off. GPR-assisted regression analysis maps complex electrolyte formulations to synaptic nonlinearity, identifying an optimized NaCl·Na-TFSI binary configuration. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggest distinct intrinsic ion-association tendencies between Na+–Cl– and Na+–TFSI– pairs, consistent with the observed doping and relaxation behaviors: strongly associated Na+–Cl– pairs suppress abrupt doping to optimize linearity, reducing nonlinearity by up to ∼6-fold compared with single-anion controls, while weakly associated Na+–TFSI– pairs facilitate ion retention to expand the dynamic range (Gmax/Gmin ∼ 103). This balanced dual-anion transport enables linear, extensible, and high-dynamic-range multistate conductance modulation. Consequently, the optimized OESTs exhibit improved LTP/D linearity, reproducible cycling, and a 94.88% MNIST recognition accuracy. These results establish predictive binary ion-association design as a general framework for controlling synaptic weight modulation in organic neuromorphic devices.

item.title: JACS: Redox-Responsive 2′-OH Acylation for Late-Stage RNA Conjugation
item.description:
Junsong Guo, Qi Shi, Ru-Yi Zhu
Covalent RNA conjugates have proved effective in basic research and therapy, yet their broader use is limited by synthetic complexity and high costs. Here, we describe a modular, redox-responsive strategy for late-stage conjugation of diverse biofunctional ligands onto RNA. We show that acylation of RNA 2′-OH groups with disulfide-containing acyl moieties enables thiol–disulfide exchange with thiol-bearing ligands, including N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc), peptides, biotin, and captopril. The resulting conjugates undergo deconjugation under reducing conditions, tracelessly regenerating native RNA and enabling recovery of RNA function. The multivalent RNA-GalNAc construct displays preferential uptake in asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)-rich cells. Installation of biotin followed by streptavidin complexation yields bulky biotinylated RNA–streptavidin complexes that shield nuclease-sensitive RNA regions and markedly enhance the nuclease resistance of both short synthetic RNA and long messenger mRNA (mRNA). This platform may expand the chemical toolbox for RNA conjugation and support the development of functionally diverse RNA conjugates.

item.title: JACS: From Chemical Complexity to Magnetic Tunability in High-Entropy Spinel Oxides
item.description:
Neha Sharma, Sushanta Mandal, Nikita Sharma, Amritpal, Sangeeta Thakur, Victor Ukleev, Chen Luo, Florin Radu, et al.
High-entropy stabilization chemistry is redefining materials design by transforming configurational disorder, arising from the deliberate incorporation of multiple principal cations, into a thermodynamic advantage that promotes phase stability and enables emergent functionalities. In this work, we investigate the evolution of magnetic ordering in spinel-type high-entropy oxides by systematically varying the cation composition of the B site within a fixed high-entropy A-site matrix (nominal composition), (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)B2O4. Upon introducing multicomponent B-site configurations, we uncover a strikingly linear dependence of the magnetic transition temperature (TC) on the TCs of the corresponding single-B-site high-entropy systems. Remarkably, this trend persists even in highly complex (Ni0.2Mg0.2Co0.2Cu0.2Zn0.2)(Cr0.2Mn0.2Fe0.2Ga0.2X0.2)2O4, X = Al and Ti. Despite the material’s extremely high degree of disorder and the absence of a dominant magnetic ion or a straightforward superexchange pathway, detailed magnetization measurements, low-temperature X-ray magnetic circular dichroism, and neutron powder diffraction studies reveal robust long-range ferrimagnetic ordering. These results reveal a predictability in ferrimagnetic high-entropy spinel oxides, where, despite extreme configurational disorder and competing interactions, robust ferrimagnetic order can arise from, rather than be hindered by, extreme configurational disorder. This establishes a pathway for predictively tuning magnetic transition temperatures in high-entropy oxides beyond conventional ordered systems.

item.title: Nano Letters: Raman-Inactive Metal–Organic Framework Nanoribbons as Plasmonic-Nanocavity Spacers and Molecular Trappers for SERS Detection
item.description:
Yi Liu, Ruiqian Zhang, Shengyan Wang, Guoliang Zhou, Shuyu Zhu, Runfang Fu, Xiaolu Zhuo, Jianfang Wang
The integration of plasmonic nanostructures with metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) has emerged as a powerful strategy to enhance the sensitivity and selectivity of surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). While the resultant hybrid systems exploit localized surface plasmon resonance for electric-field enhancement and MOF porosity for molecular enrichment, their practical applications are hindered by challenges, including intrinsic Raman interference from MOFs, precise control over MOF dimensions, and restricted plasmon coupling configurations. Herein we present a promising design featuring Raman-inactive MOF nanoribbons embedded within plasmonic nanogaps between a gold film and gold nanospheres (NSs). The sub-10 nm MOF interlayer eliminates Raman background while maximizing electromagnetic enhancement. The resultant Au-film/MOF/NSs architecture enables remarkable SERS performances with enhancement factors of 1010 across diverse molecular sizes. This work not only enriches the toolbox of MOF-based plasmonic sensing platforms, but also opens the way for further exploration into other Raman-inactive MOFs and mechanisms.

item.title: Nano Letters: Regulating the Spin-State and Frontier Orbital of a Molecular FePc Catalyst by Interlayer Electronic Coupling for Enhanced ORR Activity
item.description:
Yan Tan, Lin Ding, Aoshuang Li, Xiu-Cai Jiang, Yuhao Xia, Yiwen Cheng, Zhong Shi, Yu-Zhong Zhang, et al.
Development of efficient and durable catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction is essential for the advancement of metal–air batteries and fuel cells, yet it remains a significant challenge. Here, we present an interlayer-coupling strategy to modulate iron phthalocyanine by adjacent carbon-supported cobalt species. The resulting FePc@CoNC demonstrates superior ORR activity, with a half-wave potential of 0.927 V and achieving a peak power density of 336 mW cm–2 alongside cycling stability exceeding 1527 cycles. Density functional theory analysis reveals that the adjacent Co single atoms and Co nanoparticles synergistically enhance the localization of Fe dz2 electrons while suppressing spin polarization of Fe 3d orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes adsorption energetics of key intermediates involved in the rate-determining step, thereby accelerating ORR kinetics. These results elucidate the significance of interlayer electronic coupling in axially tuning spin states and frontier orbitals of molecular Fe–N4 centers, offering a general strategy for enhancing oxygen electrocatalysis through electronic structure engineering.

item.title: JACS: Synthesis and Characterization of the Proposed 1,4-Dihydropyridinate Intermediate with a Nickel-Pincer Nucleotide Cofactor Model Complex
item.description:
Samuel M. Bhutto, Rachel E. Siegel, Paul M. Lam, Kevin Rivera Cruz, Xiujing Xing, Brennen J. Lessard, James C. Fettinger, Hannah S. Shafaat, et al.
The nickel pincer nucleotide (NPN) cofactor was structurally characterized in lactate racemase in 2014, and it is now known that NPN is important in a superfamily of enzymes responsible for isomerization of α-hydroxyacids and also important in other hydride transfer reactions across bacteria and archaea. A decade of biochemical and theoretical studies have led to proposals for the mechanism of reaction for the NPN, but structural or spectroscopic characterization of a well-defined intermediate in the mechanisms has been elusive. Herein, we report a synthetic model of the NPN cofactor which is faithful to the cofactor in consisting of a di(thioamide) substituted pyridine ring. The hydride transfer reactivity of the NPN model was studied and both 1,4- and 1,2-dihydropyridinates (DHP–) of both the free ligand and the Ni complex have been isolated and studied spectroscopically. No evidence for Ni-hydride formation was observed. The UV–vis spectrum of the 1,4-DHP– Ni model complex (1H1,4) has features matching UV–vis spectra collected in biochemical studies where NaBH4 was added to the NPN-dependent enzyme, lactate racemase; whereas the spectra of 1-I and 1H1,2 do not match spectra collected from NPN cofactor reaction intermediates. Thus, the isolation and characterization of 1H1,4 reported herein provides the first direct experimental evidence assigning the reactivity observed in biochemical studies to the pyridyl C4 position of a NPN cofactor model complex.

item.title: JACS: Covalent Integration of Poly(α-lipoic acid) with Silicate Networks: Sustainable Hybrid Materials with Tunable Properties
item.description:
Basim Basheer, Zhibin Guan
The development of sustainable organic–inorganic hybrid materials with a molecular level of covalent integration remains a major challenge. Here, we report a one-pot synthesis of covalently integrated poly(α-lipoic acid)-silicate (PLAOH·SiO2) hybrid networks using α-lipoic acid, an abundant natural building block, and complementary silicate precursors. Strategic selection of silicate precursors enables direct Si–O–C covalent bonding with hydroxyl groups on the poly(α-lipoic acid) backbone, yielding molecularly integrated, single-phase hybrid materials across varied organic-to-inorganic ratios. Systematic compositional variation enables continuous tuning of mechanical properties (Young’s modulus: 0.94 ± 0.03 – 63.3 ± 5.67 MPa, Hardness: 1.14 ± 0.07 – 73.10 ± 8.81 MPa) while preserving optical transparency (>75% transmittance) and thermal stability (Td > 220 °C) across the entire series. The hybrid material can be reprocessed and chemically recycled to the monomer. This provides a practical synthesis of sustainable hybrid materials with tunable mechanical properties, addressing critical needs in sustainable advanced materials manufacturing.

item.title: JACS: An N-Heterocyclic Imine-Supported Two-Coordinate 1,2-Bis(borinium) Dication
item.description:
Ke Li, Arseni Kostenko, Burkhard Butschke, Daniel Franz, Tobias Weng, Shigeyoshi Inoue
Two-coordinate diboron(II) dications represent highly electron-deficient species that deviate substantially from the classical octet rule. Their extreme electrophilicity, significant Coulombic repulsion, and inherent instability render their isolation particularly challenging, leaving them hitherto elusive. Herein, we report an N-heterocyclic imine (NHI)-supported formal 1,2-bis(borinium) dication, an isoelectronic analogue of the diberyllocene, featuring a unique B(sp)–B(sp) bonding motif devoid of σ-donor stabilization and free from counterion and solvent interactions. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis reveals that the resulting two-coordinate diboron(II) dication adopts a nearly linear −C–N–B–B–N–C– arrangement. DFT calculations suggest that it is best described as an N≡B–B≡N core, with two B≡N-type units linked by a B–B single bond and capped by imidazolium-type rings, with two vacant π*(B–N) orbitals localized at the boron atoms. Reactivity studies further establish that this species behaves as a Lewis superacid, capable of small molecule activation and functions as an efficient precatalyst to promote diverse catalytic transformations under mild conditions.

item.title: JACS: Reprogramming ThDP-Dependent Enzyme for Intermolecular [3 + 2] Annulation via a Homoenolate Intermediate
item.description:
Huimin Liu, Yinhong Lai, Huangong Li, Xuesi Chen, Lintao Pan, Tiantian Liu, Zekun He, Jingyu Zhang, et al.
Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)-dependent enzymes are versatile biocatalysts for carbon–carbon bond formation, yet their catalytic repertoire has been largely confined to linear homologation and intramolecular cyclizations that rely on single-site reactive intermediates such as the Breslow or ketyl radical species. Intermolecular annulation─a powerful strategy for constructing cyclic architectures─has remained elusive within this enzyme class. Here, we report the first intermolecular [3 + 2] annulation catalyzed by a ThDP-dependent enzyme, achieved through a homoenolate-mediated nucleophilic addition pathway. A phylogeny-guided enzyme mining identified a previously uncharacterized enzyme from Variovorax boronicumulans(ThDP-5), and subsequent protein engineering yielded the F484S variant, which exhibits markedly enhanced activity and exquisite stereocontrol. This biocatalytic system exhibits a broad substrate scope (30 examples), accommodating diverse substituted cinnamaldehydes and isatins to afford chiral spirooxindole lactones with excellent stereoselectivity (up to > 20:1 dr and 99% ee). Preparative-scale reactions (2 mmol) validate its synthetic utility. This work expands ThDP-dependent biocatalysis to intermolecular annulations, providing a robust and selective platform for the construction of pharmaceutically relevant spirocyclic architectures.

item.title: JACS: Electron-Catalyzed Supramolecular Assembly with High Efficiency, Robustness, and Versatility
item.description:
Guangcheng Wu, Qinghua Yang, Yunyan Qiu, Long Zhang, Quentin Stern, Hongliang Chen, Kang Cai, Xueze Zhao, et al.
Although catalysis is widely exploited by nature to orchestrate noncovalent supramolecular assembly and build up complex living systems, its utilization in synthetic chemistry has conventionally been limited to accelerating covalent reactions. Consequently, the development of artificial systems for catalytic assembly remains a formidable and largely unexplored challenge. Here, we present a rationally designed strategy of electron-catalyzed supramolecular assembly, wherein the electron acts as an efficient, robust, and versatile catalyst to accelerate the formation of a donor–acceptor complex. Optimization of the elementary steps and intermediate stability yields an efficient catalytic cycle, furnishing the process with both a high turnover number and operational robustness in open air. Furthermore, the electron catalysis can be readily triggered by diverse external stimuli─including electricity, light, and mechanical force─enabling precise spatiotemporal control over the assembly process and near-quantitative synthesis of supramolecular complexes. Collectively, this work establishes a well-elucidated strategy of catalytic assembly with remarkable practicality, advancing the frontiers of noncovalent synthetic chemistry.

item.title: JACS: Mapping the Slow Propagation of Disorder across a Photoreceptor’s Tertiary Structure with Time-Resolved Crystallography
item.description:
Nicolas Caramello, Yuhei Hosokawa, Kai-Chun Yang, Po-Hsun Wang, Sylvain Engilberge, Pei-Jyun Liu, Yu-Chen Chang, Thierry Giraud, et al.
Order–disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. We applied time-resolved serial oscillation crystallography to establish the structural kinetics of the light-triggered order–disorder transition of an animal-like cryptochrome as a six-second-long molecular movie with near-atomic all-residue spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Our 29 structural snapshots mapped the propagation of disorder across the tertiary structure motifs of a cryptochrome’s C-terminal region, triggered by a single broken D321–R492 salt bridge. The order–disorder transition followed a nucleation-propagation mechanism reminiscent of helix–coil dynamics and proceeded over up to five seconds, with regions distal to the D321–R492 trigger initially undergoing slow zero-order disordering before switching to first-order unfolding kinetics. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order–disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.

item.title: JACS: A Single Water Molecule Drives a 20-Fold Acceleration in the Gas-Phase Reaction of Iodide with Ozone
item.description:
Samuel C. Brydon, Péter Szabó, David L. Marshall, Adam J. Trevitt, Evan J. Bieske, Jeremy N. Harvey, Stephen J. Blanksby
Iodine chemistry has an outsized role in the atmosphere and environment due to its highly reactive nature. Unlike chlorine and bromine, around 80% of atmospheric iodine is emitted directly from the ocean through the reaction of iodide and ozone at the sea surface. Uncertainties remain, however, in the effects of hydration, salinity, temperature, and other factors on this globally significant reaction. Using linear ion-trap mass spectrometry, a single water molecule is shown here to provide a 23 (±6)-fold acceleration to the rate of iodide oxidation. The first step in reaction of both I– and I–·H2O with ozone is oxidation to IO– with subsequent fast reactions to yield IO3–. No evidence is found for direct routes from I–·H2O to IO2– nor any incorporation of the water oxygen into ionic products. Ab initio calculations show that the initial rate-determining step for both reactions proceeds on the singlet surface with water playing an active role to lower the barrier through hydrogen bonding. Kinetic modeling based on the computed energetics is in excellent agreement with experimental measurements and enables extrapolation of this reaction to lower temperatures relevant to polar regions and the ozone layer. This analysis shows that (i) I– may outcompete I• for ozone destruction as temperature decreases, and (ii) I–·H2O reacts more than an order of magnitude faster than I• over 350 to 230 K. This work demonstrates that iodide has a previously underappreciated role in multiphase ozone destruction in the atmosphere and lays the foundation for understanding microscopic environmental influences in salt clusters and nanodroplets.

item.title: JACS: Control of Charge Carrier Dynamics and Bandgap Renormalization in CdS Quantum Dot Hybrids by Interface Polarity
item.description:
Shrabanti Mondal, Uttam Chowdhury, Subhajit Dey, Anik Ratan Das, Mohit Chaudhary, Pabitra Chattopadhyay, Andrey S. Vasenko, Ritabrata Sarkar, et al.
Charge carrier dynamics in wurtzite CdS quantum dots (QDs) form the basis for applications in optoelectronics and photocatalysis. We demonstrate that the quantum dynamics, energy gaps, and energy level alignments at CdS QD interfaces can be controlled by the polarity of the CdS QD surface. By performing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations within a density-functional tight-binding framework, we demonstrate a strong dependence of photoinitiated processes in CdS QDs/graphene nanoribbon (GNR) hybrids on interface polarity. At room temperature, hole transfer is accelerated by a factor of 2 and exciton lifetime is enhanced by nearly an order of magnitude when the CdS QD surface is switched from polar to nonpolar. Remarkably, the interfacial bandgap for the polar QD/GNR hybrid is reduced to half upon heating from 0 K to room temperature, while it remains nearly unchanged for the nonpolar hybrid. At an intermediate temperature, the ultrafast charge separation is maintained; however, charge recombination shows the opposite trend relative to room temperature. The polar interface exhibits a longer lifetime than the nonpolar interface, due to weakened electron–phonon Fröhlich interaction and decreased gap renormalization. The strong and highly nonlinear dependence of bandgap renormalization and carrier dynamics on temperature in the polar QD/GNR hybrid is associated with significant structural reconstruction, which is absent in the nonpolar counterpart. The demonstrated control of excited-state processes by interface polarity and the strong dependence of the dynamics and energy level alignment on temperature provide key fundamental insights for informed design of modern materials for optoelectronics and energy conversion.

item.title: Nano Letters: Hierarchical Ionic Programming of Stretchable Organic Electrochemical Transistors for Dual-Mode Sensing and Computing
item.description:
Benfei Xu, Yuzhe Gu, Xuan Zhu, Xiaotian Wang, Baoguang Liu, Yang Li
Organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) are promising building blocks for flexible in-sensor computing, yet the conflicting ionic dynamic demands of high-fidelity sensing and nonvolatile memory remain challenging to reconcile within a unified hardware platform. Here, we report a hierarchical compositional programming strategy that addresses this trade-off across a standardized stretchable OECT architecture. Regulating 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl (TEMPO)-oxidized cellulose nanofiber content in poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT) tunes channel capacitance and mechanical compliance, while tailoring the supramolecular network in a deep eutectic solvent gel electrolyte dictates ion retention kinetics. This strategy establishes distinct operational regimes via tailored formulations: a rapidly reversible, low-hysteresis state for sensing and a persistent ion trapping state for neuromorphic computing. The sensing OECT enables real-time electrocardiogram acquisition with a 35.6 dB signal-to-noise ratio and 98.9% biometric identification accuracy across 15 subjects. The computing state supports temporal Morse code demodulation and Pavlovian associative learning, demonstrating application-adaptive stretchable bioelectronics.

item.title: JACS: Low-Temperature-Mediated Lamellar–Micelle Assembly of Wrinkled Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Aligned Pores and High Interconnectivity
item.description:
Lu Liu, Yanyan Yu, Borui Yang, Jialong Li, Haotian Zhou, Lanhao Yang, Niling Lou, Qianqian Lu, et al.
Mesoporous structures with highly permeable channels are of great significance for fast diffusion; however, the delicate engineering of straightforward pores remains quite limited, with most of mesostructures are tortuous pores derived from spherical micelle assembly. Herein, we explore a novel lamellar–micelle assembly approach that enables to generate a type of wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres with highly interconnected divergent mesopores. In place of the conventional spherical micelles, the key for controlling such unusual assembly is determined by the construction of laminar micelles (copolymer L121/F127 composite) and heterogeneous growth on sedimented F127 seeds at a low temperature of 5 °C. The fabricated wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres after template removal possess a particle size at ∼910 nm, a high surface area of 315 m2 g–1, a uniform pore size at 36 nm, as well as radial mesochannels with high interconnectivity up to 96%. Further regulation on the reaction temperature and template ratio allows for a high tunability over the pore size and wrinkle degree. When employed as a sodium storage anode, the radially aligned large-pore structure drastically facilitates charge transport and electrolyte penetration, thus delivering rate capability (142 mAh g–1 at 10 A g–1) and long-term cyclability (90.5% retention after 1000 cycles at 2 A g–1) compared to commercial hard carbon. Our work underscores a particular assembly pathway through lamellar micelles as an effective approach for building up ultrafast mesopore highways toward promising diffusion-related applications.

item.title: JACS: Specific Amino Acid Imaging of Protein Condensates in Live Cells by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
item.description:
Ruifeng Sun, Ruowei Zhang, Fanghao Hu
Intracellular protein condensates formed by liquid–liquid phase separation have gained increasing attention in recent years due to their key roles in many physiological and pathological processes. However, fluorescence imaging of protein condensates is limited by the bulky fluorescent tags that could perturb the protein localization and interaction. Imaging techniques that can visualize protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbations remain lacking. Here, we develop a strategy to image intracellular protein condensates by coupling stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy to specific amino acid labeling. Different types of amino acids are found to exhibit distinct incorporation patterns in the live cells. By metabolic labeling of deuterated tyrosine-d4 and arginine-d7, ALS-related fused in sarcoma (FUS) protein condensates can be visualized with a high specificity. In addition, two-color pulse-chase imaging reveals protein translation arrest in FUS condensates under stress conditions. Furthermore, heterogeneous tyrosine phosphorylation is imaged in live cells and FUS condensates based on the Raman blue shift of phosphorylated tyrosine-d4. Thus, our technique to image specific amino acids by SRS provides a new platform to visualize the metabolic turnover and post-translational modifications of protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbation.

item.title: ACS Nano: Competing Surface Dynamics of Copper Catalyst Particles during Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Reduction
item.description:
Yifan Chen, Tom Burwell, Madasamy Thangamuthu, Sadegh Ghaderzadeh, Gazi N. Aliev, Haytham E. M. Hussein, Sean Hoggett, Michael W. Fay, et al.
Copper is a powerful catalyst for the electrochemical carbon dioxide reduction reaction (CO2RR), but it faces challenges with selectivity and stability dependent on its structural characteristics. We developed a platform that combines graphitized carbon nanofibers with identical-location transmission electron microscopy (IL-TEM) to study individual copper nanoparticles at the atomic scale under various reaction conditions. Notably, we observed that competing phenomena such as Ostwald ripening, coalescence, selective etching, and Coulomb-explosion-like fragmentation coexist in the same reaction area, with the latter being qualitatively consistent with a charge-driven fission pathway in larger nanoparticles (>10 nm). By tracking uniquely identifiable nanoparticles both individually and in groups, our findings focus on the range of surface-confined restructuring pathways during CO2RR. This contrasts with solution-mediated phenomena, such as dissolution–precipitation, which dominate under open-circuit potential (OCP) and significantly destabilize the catalyst prior to the reaction, highlighting the importance of eliminating this effect. Under CO2RR conditions, Cu nanoparticles are highly sensitive to subtle variations in the support’s nanotexture, defects, and electronic structure, leading to the coexistence of counteracting mechanisms we observed. These observations provide a structural framework for understanding the dynamic behavior of copper-on-carbon catalysts under CO2RR conditions, guiding the development of strategies to improve catalyst stability and performance.

item.title: JACS: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
item.description:
Yiwen Liu, Xiaoya Zhao, Zhang Wen, Bingxuan Du, Yu Shi, Lunjie Qin, Wei Li, Haoshen Zhou, et al.
Lithium–air batteries suffer from moisture-induced parasitic reactions and electrolyte evaporation in ambient air. A fundamental challenge is the “micro-size inversion” paradox, where H2O (0.275 nm) is smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), rendering conventional size-based sieving ineffective. Here, we report a composite membrane composed of polydimethylsiloxane and fluorinated vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-VF) to break this selectivity barrier. By grafting 1H,1H,2H,2H-perfluorodecyl groups onto a vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-V), we establish a surface-chemistry-driven sieving mechanism. This design creates a molecular-level hydrogen-bond-repellent barrier that specifically inhibits polar H2O penetration while maintaining high nonpolar O2 flux, effectively decoupling the permeability-hydrophobicity trade-off. Molecular dynamics simulations corroborate this mechanism, demonstrating that the COF-VF exhibits significantly reduced adsorption affinity toward H2O compared to the pristine COF-V. In 40% RH ambient air, the battery equipped with this membrane delivers a discharge capacity of 3596 mAh g–1 and sustains cycling for 2700 h (270 cycles), a 10.8-fold improvement over unprotected cells. Advanced characterizations via DRT and DEMS confirm that the membrane promotes reversible Li2O2 formation and significantly suppresses LiOH accumulation. This work provides a multiscale strategy for molecular-level selective separation in practical energy storage.

item.title: JACS: Role of (Co)substrate Coordination to Iron in Activating Its Two-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen: Mechanism of Pterin Activation in Tryptophan Hydroxylase
item.description:
Robert R. Gipson, Ting C. Lin, Dory E. DeWeese, David F. Nielsen, Günther H. J. Peters, Edward I. Solomon
Many O2-activating mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes require substrate or cofactor/cosubstrate coordination to iron to form the key peroxy-bridged intermediate necessary for catalysis with no net change in the iron redox state. The role of (co)substrate coordination, however, remained unclear. Here, we leverage a pterin-dependent enzyme, tryptophan hydroxylase, for which cosubstrate (pterin) coordination can be experimentally controlled by the absence and presence of substrate, to explicitly determine the role of pterin coordination in O2 binding and peroxo formation. EPR, absorption, circular dichroism, and magnetic circular dichroism spectroscopies on the {FeNO}7 analog of the unobservable {FeO2}8 intermediate without and with pterin coordination demonstrate that pterin coordination induces new absorption bands and enhances NO affinity by 3.6 kcal mol–1 at 277 K. These new bands are pterin-to-iron ligand-to-metal charge-transfer transitions that compensate the electron donation from iron to NO upon NO binding. Extension of our findings on {FeNO}7 to {FeO2}8 evidences that pterin coordination stabilizes O2 binding and facilitates the two-electron transfer from pterin to {FeO2}8 to reduce the transition-state barrier for peroxo formation by 12.7 kcal mol–1, corresponding to a 1010 increase in reaction rate. The electron transfer pathways established herein underscore a unified mechanism for the pterin-dependent, α-ketoglutarate-dependent, extradiol, and intradiol dioxygenase families of mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes through which (co)substrate coordination enhances O2 binding via one-electron transfer within {FeO2}8 and two-electron donation from the (co)substrate (one to bound O2 and one to iron) to generate the peroxo species with no net redox change on the iron.

item.title: JACS: Solvent/Anion Codepleted Solvation Engineering Enables Low-Coordination Electrolytes for High-Energy and Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells
item.description:
Xinhong Hu, Qinhao Shi, Jinyu Wan, Meiyi Zhang, Yongfeng Zhao, Zi-Feng Ma, Yang Si, Pengyan Wang, et al.
Widespread deployment of sodium-ion batteries demands both high energy density and reliable low-temperature (LT) operation, but is constrained by a persistent trade-off between high-voltage stability (cathode/electrolyte) and LT ion-transport kinetics. Herein, we report a solvent/anion codepleted solvation engineering strategy to construct low-coordination electrolytes through competitive anion complexation mediated by a bulky electron-deficient additive, TMSB (tris(trimethylsilyl)borate). We reveal that TMSB preferentially complexes with PF6– to suppress direct anion-Na+ coordination, while its bulky steric backbone disrupts conventional ion-pair networks and restricts excessive solvent-Na+ coordination. This strategy fundamentally boosts ionic conductivity (from 2.41 to 5.34 mS cm–1) and lowers the desolvation energy barrier (from 44.82 to 33.97 kJ mol–1). Moreover, such a strategy enables a high-modulus (2.7 GPa), inorganic-rich cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI), which can not only mitigate surface degradation, but also suppress bulk phase transitions of cathode materials. Consequently, the electrolyte demonstrates broad compatibility across diverse cathodes (NFM, NVP, and P2-NNMO) under extreme voltage (up to 4.5 V) and temperature (−40 to 25 °C) conditions. Remarkably, the scaled-up 6.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a record-high energy density of 200 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C, while maintaining 162 Wh kg–1 even at −20 °C, offering a generalizable molecular paradigm for extreme-environment energy storage.

item.title: ACS Nano: Accelerating the Discovery of Synthesizable 2D Hybrid Double Perovskites through Human–LLM Collaborative Descriptor Engineering
item.description:
Rong Guo, Chang-Feng Wang, Ming-Gang Ju, Yilei Wu, Peiguo Liu, Qionghua Zhou, Shuaihua Lu, Zhilong Song, et al.
Two-dimensional hybrid perovskites offer exceptional structural diversity and multifunctional properties, yet their synthesis remains a major bottleneck due to low hit rates and strong reliance on empirical intuition. Here we introduce AL-SynAgent, a human-in-the-loop, ML-guided screening workflow that integrates literature-derived synthetic priors, expert-refined chemical descriptors, and active learning to assess the synthesis feasibility of two dimensional (2D) hybrid organic–inorganic rare-earth double perovskites (HORDPs). By converting LLM-assisted literature knowledge and expert chemical reasoning into system-specific computable descriptors, AL-SynAgent reduces dependence on large experimental data sets while retaining chemically interpretable decision rules. With experimental feedback from only 4.8% of candidate space, the model converged and achieved successful target-phase formation for 11 of the 14 candidates in the prospectively selected experimental set, corresponding to a hit rate of 78.6%. Screening of an enumerated virtual library of 280,000 candidates further prioritized 64,482 compositions with high predicted synthesis feasibility. Notably, three newly obtained compounds also exhibit both excellent ferroelectricity and photoluminescence, including (4-F-321)4RbEu(NO3)8, which displays an exceptionally high Curie temperature of 388 K and strong emission at 592 nm. This work establishes a practical, human-in-the-loop strategy for data-efficient prioritization of candidate compositions within chemically constrained 2D HORDP space under a standardized laboratory synthesis protocol.

item.title: ACS Nano: Engineered Living Materials: A Therapeutic Paradigm beyond Conventional Biomaterials
item.description:
Lan Yang, Jiawei Lu, Shiqi Huang, Ling Zhang
Development of biomaterials in the past two decades has profoundly advanced modern medicine. However, the relatively simple and insufficiently biological functions and lack of self-renewal capability limit their ability to dynamically adapt to complex physiological environments. Engineered living materials (eLMs) use living organisms as core functional units and provide a therapeutic approach for addressing these limitations. Thus, this review systematically summarizes the recent advancements in eLMs, beginning with an overview of the primary biological chassis, including bacteria, microalgae, fungi, and mammalian cells. eLMs hold the valuable capabilities of long-term self-sustainment and self-proliferation within complex biological environments, which are endowed with intelligent regulation. For instance, they can sense environmental signals and execute programmed functional outputs, including therapeutic protein secretion or targeted migration. Moreover, they achieve precise control over therapeutic actions, encompassing spatial localization at the disease site, temporal dynamics of the intervention, and quantitative regulation of outputs. Furthermore, we highlight the broad therapeutic applications of these dynamic systems in addressing complex diseases. Finally, we discuss the current translational challenges and future directions of the field, emphasizing the potential of integrating artificial intelligence with synthetic biology and nanomaterial engineering to develop next-generation programmable eLMs and expand their utility across diverse sectors.

item.title: JACS: General Synthesis of Functionalized 1,3-Diamines from Azoarenes and Enoates via Electrochemical Annulation and N–N Bond Cleavage Followed by Chemical Reduction
item.description:
Xinyu Chen, Yanping Sun, Pierre. H. Dixneuf, Huanfeng Jiang, Min Zhang
Despite the widespread utility of N-substituted 1,3-diamines across numerous fields, their selective synthesis directly from readily available feedstocks remains a long-standing challenge. In this context, we report a room-temperature electrochemical protocol for the synthesis of both symmetrical and unsymmetrical N,N′-disubstituted 1,3-diamines through electrochemical transformation of azoarenes with enoates, followed by convergent reduction of the resulting β-amino amides. This method features broad substrate scope, operational simplicity, no need for noble transition-metal catalysts, and high chemoselectivity. Mechanistic studies indicate that the reaction is initiated by the reduction of azoarenes, facilitated by HCOOH, while Zn2+ ions leached from anodic oxidation serve as a Lewis acid to promote intramolecular cyclization via ester amidation. Subsequent cathodic reduction drives N–N bond cleavage to afford the β-amino amide intermediates, thereby endowing azoarenes with dual-nitrogen synthon capability.
